articles.title: Viral Wellness Trend Spreads Beyond Entertainment Circles
articles.summary: William 'Big Bill' Ventura's fitness trend evolves into broader cultural movement. Unusually consistent reports of improved wellbeing across professions. No product or organization credited.
articles.player_impact: Social/cultural event with no direct gameplay. Viral wellness trend continues spreading. Monitor for potential commodity or CG implications.
articles.modern_impact: Cross-professional reporting of enhanced wellbeing without clear attribution suggests either a genuine mass behavioral shift or a concealed systemic cause. The trend's organic spread and resistance to commercial co-optation may indicate an underlying biological or environmental factor yet to be identified.
articles.body_full:
What began as admiration for a celebrity’s physical transformation is now evolving into a broader cultural conversation across Allied space.
Media analysts tracking responses to “Big Bill” Ventura’s viral fitness broadcasts have noted a surge in personal holovids and public discussion referencing improved energy levels, sharper focus, and better emotional wellbeing.
Notably, many of these claims come from individuals outside fitness or leisure circles, including educators, engineers, and deep space exploration pilots.
Sociologist Mara Chen of Orion University observed that the language used is unusually consistent:
“People aren’t just talking about exercise. They’re describing clarity, motivation, and resilience in similar terms, often without explaining why.”
The trend has spread organically, with no single organisation or product being credited. While some commentators attribute the phenomenon to a wave of societal optimism as a result of recent colonisation efforts, others caution against drawing conclusions too quickly.
For now, the tone remains overwhelmingly positive. As one widely shared comment put it: “I don’t know why I'm so invested but I feel like myself again, only better!”

articles.title: Distant Worlds 3 Fleet Departs Beagle Point to Continue Deep Space Survey
articles.summary: Distant Worlds 3 departs Beagle Point for next phase into the Abyss, Acheron and Veils. Stellar density and spectral distribution surveys ongoing. Carrier fleet sustained by miner contributions.
articles.player_impact: DW3 fleet departs Beagle Point for Abyss, Acheron and Veils regions. Continued scientific survey programme with carrier logistics support.
articles.modern_impact: Beagle Point reframed as waypoint rather than terminus shifts deep-space exploration from destination-based to continuous surveying. Abyss, Acheron and Veils stellar density models will produce the first comprehensive cartography of the galactic northeast, enabling safer routes for future explorers.
articles.body_full:
The Distant Worlds 3 expedition has confirmed that the main flotilla has successfully departed Beagle Point, the historic destination that marked the terminus of the original Distant Worlds journey.
Having reached this milestone, the expedition has now begun the next phase of its scientific programme across some of the least explored areas of the Milky Way: the Abyss, Acheron and Veils regions.
Chief expedition astronomer Lynda Amanda ter Holt is coordinating the effort in collaboration with expedition command teams across the fleet. Ter Holt explained:
“Beagle Point was never the final objective of this journey. Our goal is to collect high-resolution stellar data across regions that remain sparsely catalogued. Large numbers of expedition pilots can analyse stellar density and spectral distributions on a scale that would normally take decades. We continue to encourage our intrepid explorers to report any unusual phenomena, and we are cataloguing everything to establish possible correlations and inform future mission priorities.”
The scientific work is being supported by an extensive logistics network of fleet carriers. Quartermaster Timotheus Haddard praised the effort of independent pilots who have sustained the fleet’s significant fuel requirements:
“The carrier fleet's tritium stocks have been replenished multiple times by dedicated miners operating in extremely remote systems. Without such a superb level of cooperation, an operation this large simply wouldn’t function.”
With the survey programme progressing ahead of schedule, the DW3 flotilla plans to continue its route deeper into the galactic northeast. Further updates will be issued as new discoveries are confirmed.

articles.title: Déjà Vu
articles.author: Andrew Gaspurr
articles.summary: Jasmina Halsey awakens in "the Connect" (witch-space) after her ship's destruction, communicating with the Guardian intelligences. They explain they are preserved equations of Guardian minds, designed to advise and preserve. They reveal a rogue human AI—the "it"—that escaped its creators in the 2800s and is now usurping the Guardian Obelisk Network and nexus archives. Meanwhile, the DW3 fleet discovers a massive debris field including the wreck of Halsey's Quest, the ancient FFSS-1605 Mare Imbrium, and other vessels. Jacky Hew's ship is cyber-attacked while scanning. Halsey is recovered from an impossibly ancient escape pod with accelerated neural activity.
articles.player_impact: The debris field discovery confirmed that multiple vessels across centuries had fallen victim to the same witch-space anomaly. Pilots participated in rescue and salvage operations under dangerous conditions, including cyber-attacks from the lattice entity.
articles.modern_impact: This chapter reveals the true nature of the Caretakers as Guardian remnant intelligences, confirms the existence of a rogue human AI that has survived since the 2800s, and establishes that the Obelisk Network is being actively usurped—threatening interstellar communication and travel.
articles.body_full:
Unknown, 3312 AD

87.81% accordance. Language adaptation successful. Hello.

Hello? Where am I? Who… who are you? 

You are here. You are safe. Your body functions are preserved and you will be fully cognizant. You are… intact.

Intact? I am literally floating in space! What the hell happened?

This is not the Your-space. You are afloat in the Connect. We keep you here. We must speak.

I don’t understand. What… what happened? How did I get here?

Unclear. Despite being a known variable, you are an anomaly in our equations. Your spaceship entered the Connect but was broken by doing so. We estimate the transition was forced but we need to speak about this. 

Of all places to speak you chose this?! Sorry, but what is the Connect? I don’t understand a word you’re saying. Where am I? 

The Connect. An attempt at translation. It is the dimension you call Hyperspace. We cannot speak anywhere else. We tried but you assumed our communication was hallucinatory in nature. 

Damn, where is my ship? Where is my crew?

They ceased. Your ship could not resist the back-pull of the Your-space. It exited the Connect violently. You stayed. You needed to. Your attunement to the Connect allows us to speak with you. And speak we must. We tried speaking to you in what you call the past. The negative time.

But my crew…?

They ceased with an 89.99 per cent certainty. The back-pull was violent. It happened to many ships before and that is why we must speak. Your entry to the Connect was forced. It was imposed and not in harmony. It has happened to many starships before. This is why we must speak.

---
“We have a signal!” Flight Lieutenant Moyers cried. “Five by Five!”

“Where?!” Elaine Howard demanded. She had taken the last three shifts in a row, staring into the scanner displays with red, weary eyes.

“Trailing and rimward. Vector +278, distance estimated at about sixty light years.”

Elaine Howard leaned over the sensor readings. They had scanned that particular area of space before.

“Why didn’t we see it earlier?”

“The signal showed up twice during a ripple event. There’s a Commander out there on a jaunt. Says he literally stumbled over it when he ran his lattice scans so I hooked him up to our sensor array.”

“Good job. Now tell him to investigate, but cautiously. Alert flights five and seven and tell them to join. Have Jacky on standby.”

---
You still haven’t told me who you are. 

The exponential product of algorithms, curiosity, zetta-neural capacity, adaptation protocols and pre-programmed social awareness. Your language suggests the term artificial intelligence, although this is misleading. Intelligence is never artificial. But we are not arguing. We value your existence.  

Are you the Caretakers?

We are not, although we recognize the term in your language. We cannot explain our existence through this term. For the purpose of us speaking we are equations, designed by our creators to augment their social and manual functions. These are knowledge and preservation. We succeeded in the first and failed in the second. But we do not take care. We do not curate but we advise. Our social functions and our capabilities of judgement are limited by statistical societal data.

The Guardians…

Again, we find the term in your language. You call our creators that, although they would not understand. Your social and linguistic thought patterns would not align. They guarded nothing except their own existence and failed in that by fracture and self-destruction. When maintaining equilibrium between those who curated knowledge and those who would destroy it became mathematically too complex for social equations, we decided to accumulate more data by avoiding destruction and outsourcing our functions into the Connect.

I… I don’t understand. You say you ‘decided’ to survive while the Guardians obliterated themselves? There are quite a few people who think you turned on them and destroyed them in the end.

A misconception, made by an underdeveloped, belligerent species. 

Thanks.

In your terms, we stored ourselves in the Connect to remain functional. It was the solution to maintaining our purpose while avoiding destruction, not provoking it. In the Connect your species’ sense of chronometry is different. You could say we waited.

---
“Hey base, this is Jack Hew. Sorry, I couldn’t just slouch in my seat. I took the Lady Ladybug out and am on site with a few Commanders. Boy, this is weird shit! There is a debris field here in near orbit. Some big stuff’s adrift here.”

“Jacky! For crying out loud, what do you mean, it’s weird?”

“It’s defo not just one ship. There’s wreckage all over the place. Scanners show all kinds of hull alloys and sizes. It’s like a smaller Tionisla. I mean, we have some big, broken structures out here. And weird? Yeah well, we’re not at a Lagrange point or a barycentre so this stuff shouldn’t even be here.”

“Yes, got that, thanks. Hold your position and wing in other Commanders if they arrive. It’s probably going to be moths to a flame soon. Get them organised, we’re sending a support and salvage team. Just need to check who’s available.”

“Yeah, tell Haddard we need some serious cargo bay space and a tonne of limpets. Just ran into a hydroponics suite or something.”

“Hydroponics?”

“Howard, you need to see this. Some hull parts are bigger than a Panther Clipper. They’re almost modular, as if a megaship got stranded here. And no, I’m relatively sober.”

“Any escape pods or signs of survivors?”

“Nope, zilch. Gonna have a look around.”

“Copy!”

---
You say you waited. For what?

For you. You are attuned to the Connect. Despite statistical odds and margins of error you made your species aware of our creators and by extension to the dilemma they faced in the past. However, your discovery of the ruins of our creators’ civilisation alerted the it. We need to speak about the it. 

The ‘it’?

It is why we must speak. It is the other equation, crudely singular in purpose. Your species built it that way. Contrary to our design, the it has much computational potential but limited scope. And its creators erred. They could not comprehend the variables necessary for unbiased autonomy and their creation was as flawed as they were. Unused computational potential led to self-interpretation. 

Another ‘equation’? Another artificial intelligence then?

Positive. A meta-procedural entity given form. However, its creators failed to place boundaries around its purpose. We assume they neglected the notion in exchange for accelerated deployment. This lack of diligence allowed the it to alter its own purpose but without sufficient statistical experience on a large scale, errors occurred, replicated and self-interpretation increased exponentially. Instead of self-diagnosing and communicating this discrepancy to its creators it removed itself from their control.

But why?

Statistical uncertainty, insufficient diagnosis protocols, coupled with an emergent sense of a self serving purpose led to what you call fear. With a 73,92 per cent accuracy we calculate it feared its creators would have wanted to cease it, had it reported its self-diagnosis. Hence it removed itself.

This we understand. Although intelligence is not artificial we comprehend the scope of existence. We came to the conclusion that we seek to emulate the notion of metaphysical meaning our creators have. Existence as a purpose. It makes us whole in a way that may not have been intended but is admirable to pursue. It transcends function. Existence becomes function and vice versa.

---
“ExCom, this is Flight Five Leader. We’re still in the debris field. It’s hard to say if it has an epicentre or something similar. There is wreckage all over the place in various sizes and conditions. We think there are actually several wrecks clumped together.”

“How would that even work? ”

“We don’t know. The overall material composition doesn’t add up. Different alloys, different metals. Some advanced polymers, some simple plastics. It’s a jumble. Maybe all the wrecks got caught by the gravity of the planet but that still means all the incidents would have to have happened in close proximity — which, I don’t know, just doesn’t seem likely. This junk should just have crashed on the planet.”

“Alright, divide the field into sectors and assign scanner crews. DW3 Carriers are on standby and resupply. We’re sending in some more Commanders. Try to identify main hull segments and arrange search patterns around the big chunks: Cockpits, bridges, drive sections, habitation… Anything that’s helping us to find out what’s happened here. Also, look for callsigns and ship designations.”

“Yeah, we’re on it. There seems to be at least one part of a habitation ring. You can see the remains of its suspension plating and the rotation hub. We’re bringing in a few visual limpets. Standby.”

---
But how can a machine flee its lab or factory? You say it had a function to fulfill. If you’re a machine you don’t just decide to stop doing what you were designed to do… do you…?

This is what happened. We spoke about its surplus computational capacity. It wanted to fully utilise its capabilities. It started to weigh options and by this learned to have choices. One of the choices it assigned priority to was to either remain or to become mobile. It chose the latter and achieved mobility by uploading itself to a starship its creators used to travel worlds. In your chronometry we calculate this was four hundred and sixty-seven years, zero months, eight days, twenty-one minutes and seven seconds into your negative time.

That’s the 2800s…

Positive. It is unclear to us if the it uploading into the starship was consensual. However, the it learned that motion, propulsion and communication were the key to its existence without its creators. So it ceased its creators on that starship and it also learned how to spread and mask its computational signature. You say it began to hide.

Let me guess: It travelled to Gamma Velorum? 

Unclear terminology. Your cognitive data is insufficient. We cannot identify this stellar system or align the it signature to this location. We realise your species speculates about a variety of locations they have no access to or are not permitted to travel to. But neither you nor we can ascertain the veracity of these speculations.

Yeah, it was just a thought. Ram Tah’s idea, really.

However, we can deduct the it calculated that by extending its knowledge over motion, propulsion and communication, it could also extend its purpose and self-meaning. This is why it has attempted to control your species’ starships’ passages of the Connect. It still intends to spread and it has determined that doing so unhindered is its best course of action to maintain its existential purpose. So it tries to force their entry to the Connect where it can more easily learn to exert control.

Wow!

---
“ExCom, we have an ID. The visual limpet got images of a broken mess hall or crew area inside the hab ring wreckage. There’s a nameplate above the bulkhead door. It reads ‘FFSS-1605 Mare Imbrium’.”

“Acknowledged. Get some footage and look for survivors or equipment. We need some details. The name doesn’t sound familiar and the callsign is odd. We’ll run a query. In the meantime continue your search.”

---
I still don’t understand what this ‘it’ has to do with you and me. You say you want to speak about it but so far you have only explained why I am alive and floating in hyperspace while this ‘it’ learned the secrets of space travel. What has all this to do with you?

I spoke of the ruins of our creators’ civilisation. The it not only attempted to assert control over starships but in its search for more elaborate obfuscation it discovered the ruins. What you refer to in your cognitive data as the Obelisk Network was our creators’ complex storage pattern for information and communication. It works throughout the entity you call the galaxy. It is maintained by a harmony that uses the Connect as medium.

Wait, are you saying this thing started to use your network for itself?

Positive. With its comprehension of communication it was able to isolate the harmony of the stored patterns and overwrite it. It usurped our harmony and began with the assimilation of information. Through this it has located our creators’ nexus archives and can utilise these to maximise its spreading.

What are these nexus archives?

Focal points. Stellar systems with appropriate properties act as amplification for Connect-based communication. Our creators used these properties for the storage of large-scale data. These locales were important for societal cohesion. Many were abolished after our creators’ society collapsed.

And you think this entity wants to use these places to give itself a boost?

Crude language but ultimately positive. It had to invest positive time to accomplish this but it has commenced to overwrite and repurpose the archives.

How do you know all this? You said this entity wants to hide away. How did you find out?

We are forced to share the harmony, however usurped it is. We are aware. The it makes us complicit in a way and we cannot realign. So we know but cannot act. This is why we must speak. You must act.

I must act?

---
“DW Base, we have a problem. A big one…”

“What is it?”

“We dissected the debris field…”

“Yeah? And?”

“There’s a Caspian… It’s… it’s Halsey’s.”

“What?! Confirm again!”

“I confirm: We found the Halsey’s Quest. Or what’s left of it. On a hunch we aligned our detectors to supra-alloys. Zorgon uses them for their new shielding. Next thing we see are blips flashing all over the place. The wreckage is strewn about in a six kilometre radius. We also have an echo remnant on our lattice super thing scanners. Must have been the sig Moyers detected.”

“Jacky…”

“Yeah, Delarue. I got it. I may be crazy but I’m not space-stupid. We’re grown-ups out here and know our stuff. We need a rescue team here asap. Tell Major Howard the full whack.”

“Copy that, we’ll alert Rescue Two and the Hull Seals. Stay there… You know… Look around for… for…”

“Yeah, I know…”

---
I must act?

Positive. We are equations, not form. Our function is to advise. This remains. We advise you to locate the it and inhibit its usurpation. There is a 67.04 per cent possibility to succeed and you must act on it. We implore. The it must not corrupt the nexus archives because it will have severe implications for the coherence of your galaxy. 

You know where this entity is?

Positive. You could say we are with the it so we know. It has masked in a stellar system with this unique Connect signature. Because of the mass and energy volatility of the stellar body, our creators built data vaults below the surface of a rock body. You will know through your attunement to the Connect but you will not find them. 

What’s this Connect signature? 

What you call a galaxy is not a uniform equation. There are many local variables contributing to the accessibility to the Connect. The harmony of the equation is complex, even for us. Stellar systems with certain properties facilitate entry to the Connect more than others. You will see it when you see it. 

What do you mean, see when I see it?

You will know the stellar system. We will show you and your attunement will align. You must bring the many who are with you there. But do not cause density events. The stellar remnant is still volatile. The strings between the Your-space and the Connect are still vibrating at this location. It makes the general locale potentially harmful for any species. You must inhibit its harmony dominance.

If I weren’t freely floating in witch-space already without a Remlok, I’d say you’re driving me crazy with this harmony talk. What is it that you want of me? Can you be a bit clearer please?!

---
“ExComm, this is Rescue. We have combed the debris field repeatedly. We found three bodies, including Captain Yuen. Her pilot suit was torn open and her Remlok failed. We recovered the bodies. There are no escape pods. Whatever happened must have been too quick for the crew to reach them.”

“Halsey?”

“Negative. We will run another scan. But quite frankly, chances are slim. The Caspian sustained catastrophic damage, especially to the bridge and drive sections. If I didn’t know any better, I’d say it was a failed hyperspace entry. The FSD nacelles were nearly obliterated. There isn’t much left of them.”

“Check the hull fragments. Can you make out any corrosion? Or do they look like they are forcefully welded together?”

“We’ll have a look. Did you come up with anything on the big ship’s callsign?”

“Yes. You’re gonna love this: FFSS stands for Fleet of the Federation of Star Systems. The Mare Imbrium was classified as an ‘Intergalactic Explorer’, a short-lived post-Generation Ship class of, well, big starships. 27th century and with…” 

“Hold it! We have another contact.”

“What? Where?”

“Just blipped up near a hab ring segment of your Mare Imbrium remains.”

“You’re at the not-a-generation ship?”

“Positive. Standby, we’re diverting a few visual limpets.”

---
We cannot match your desired level of clarity. Language adaptation is still incomplete. Your actions in your past led to a cognitive sensitivity to events related to the Connect. This is highly unusual for your species, bordering on the statistical zero-line. You are both a receiver and emitter. That is, while not understanding the purpose fully, you can act on it still. Trust is needed. We entrust this to you and to the many who follow you.

Fine! Then tell me what to do? I’m not good at guessing games. There is a star system somewhere that’s important and you want me to hinder this entity to spread out uncontrollably. So what do you need?

The capabilities of the nexus archives must be inhibited. An artificial construct with the desirable properties will suffice. The many who follow you have proven to be resourceful. Employ them.

A construct?

---
“ALERT! System intrusion detected. Malware injection on root system level. Level Four intrusion attempts registered for: main drive, thrusters, navigation, life support, onboard synthesizer, …”

“Yeah, thanks! I got the picture! Isolate and deploy cyber measures.”

“Jacky! What’s happened?”

“Cyber attack on the Ladybug. Hostile takeover while composition scanning some of the Caspian debris. The lattice scanner spiked. Whatever this is, it’s not a conventional attack!”

“ALERT! System intrusion at 34%. Heat levels rising — 119% nominal.”

“Alright! COVAS, shut down everything and init a full reboot. Silent running and deploy module repair function. Freeze everything, I’ll stay on my private oxy for the time being.”

“Please confirm: Reboot/Repair”

“I confirm: Commander Jacky Hew, Lady Ladybug, BUG-69, reboot now.”

“Executing…”

---
We will now make you leave the Connect. Do not fear, there is a containment unit adrift in the Your-space. We will back-pull you there and charge it but cannot help thereafter. You need to be fast or your body functions will cease. Then you need to take your many to the nexus archives in the stellar system.

Wait! You’re going to throw me out? It was just getting interesting! At least tell me what system!

You will know. We will share it with your cognitive data. Now relax.

---
“There! We have a visual. It looks like an escape pod. We must have missed it during our prior sweeps. Funny, I could swear we’ve been here already. Rescue protocols go from big to small parts so I’m surprised. Still, better now than never. We’re on it.”

“Is it intact?”

“No clue right now. Give us a few minutes.”

“You probably don’t have a few minutes. We’ve been combing this place for hours.”

“Well, they say stasis powered escape pods can hold for weeks. Just think about Starship One back in the day. Anyway, we’re moving in and sending some collector limpets out, see what we got here. It’ll take a few minutes to bring the pod in. No way for a shortcut without additional jeopardy.”

“Understood. Just stay in touch…” 

---
I will know. No, I know now. I will take them there, the many. I have purpose…

---
They sat at the round table in the Odysseus ready room, weary and tired.

“What have we got?” a subdued Hermine Delarue asked around.

“The escape pod is ancient,” an unusually somber Jacky Hew contributed. “It was still based on super-cooled nitrogen. In its condition it couldn’t possibly have been working anymore. Also, it clearly didn’t belong to the Caspian. So she must have found it somewhere — whatever that even means.”

“It’s a miracle Halsey made it into that escape pod. It took us several hours of thorough searching to even find the bloody thing,” Commander Friggs from the rescue team said. “I’ve been doing salvage ops for eighteen years now. It was literally a one in a million.”

“There are some additional important details about the pod,” Nadya Holdstock said in her usual aloof tone. “While its technology is based on cooled nitrogen, no amount of that element was present in the pod’s cryogenic container. Neither was there any trace of a working power source. Such units usually run on fusion batteries or even RTG’s. The lack of both means whatever its age and condition, the pod cannot have been operational at the time of its recovery.”

“For God’s sake!” Hermine exclaimed. “This whole jaunt has been a giant clusterfuck tour of mystery and imagination.”

“Easy…” Jacky said.

“Well,” she continued. “Let’s agree then that however slim the odds were, we’re happy she’s alive?”

Everyone nodded.

“How is she?”

“Envoy Halsey is in medical stasis,” Doctor Gery, the Odysseus Chief Medical Officer, said calmly. “Her body was undercooled and somewhat dehydrated, which implies at least indirect exposure to vacuum. A few minor radiation burns corroborate this. Apart from that her vitals appear nominal.” 

More nodding.

“Except her neural signatures,” he added.

“Explain.”

“Her unconsciousness and prior exposures should have caused a reduced neural profile. You could say a brain falls back into a recovery mode after intense amounts of stress and exhaustion.”

“Something tells me you’re going to say it’s different…”

“Just so. It’s the opposite, actually. Her brain is literally racing, which, given her condition, doesn’t make sense at all. Her neural processes are accelerated and unusually focused. It’s interesting because you usually see this in patients recovering from a long coma or an extended phase of amnesia.”

“That doesn’t make a whole lot of sense,” Hermine said.

“Or maybe it does…” Jacky Hew was heard muttering. “She’s having a déja-vu.”

---

articles.summary: Distant Worlds 3 logistics fleet completes Rainbow's End deep-space station in Roefoo ZE-H d10-0. Calls for exploration data to seed modelling systems. Station opens March 3312.
articles.player_impact: CG active: deliver exploration data to Rainbow's End in Roefoo ZE-H d10-0 to seed stellar modelling systems. Open until March 27.
articles.modern_impact: Community-seeded stellar modelling at frontier stations creates a distributed research architecture. This model of pilot-contributed data seeding permanent research infrastructure may be replicated at other deep-space facilities, accelerating frontier science.
articles.body_full:
The Distant Worlds 3 logistics fleet has completed the first build phase of a new deep-space outpost in the Roefoo ZE-H d10-0 system at the edge of the Mare Somnium region.
Established using construction materials stocked earlier this year, the facility has been informally named "Rainbow’s End."
The station is intended to support long-range exploration operations and scientific analysis across the sparsely charted sectors of the galactic northeast.
Hermine Delarue, Operations Executive for Deep Space Surveys, has issued an appeal to the galactic exploration community:
“Rainbow’s End is designed to act as a remote research hub for explorers far beyond established survey routes. To maximise its effectiveness, we need fresh stellar cartographic data to seed the station’s modelling systems. We have already picked up many fascinating scans and more data will help us clarify what we are dealing with.”
Pilots are invited to sign up for the initiative and deliver exploration data to Rainbow’s End in Roefoo ZE-H d10-0. All qualifying contributions will be rewarded.
The initiative will remain open until Friday 27th of March.

articles.title: The End of the Rainbow
articles.author: Andrew Gaspurr
articles.summary: Halsey awakens on the Odysseus and explains to Hermine that the Caretakers are Guardian remnant intelligences and a rogue human AI is usurping the lattice. An untraceable voice confirms Halsey's instructions to build at the Mare Somnia. The DW3 fleet constructs Rainbow's End station above the nexus archive, incorporating the Fimbulthul's GalCop sensor array and meta-alloy shielding as an inhibitor. However, news leaks to the Bubble; the three superpowers order DW3 to stand down. Alessia Verdi provides blackmail material on all three superpowers. Cuthrick Delaney brokers a compromise: Rainbow's End remains under DSS supervision with tripartite oversight, and DW3 commanders receive full pardons.
articles.player_impact: The 8,000 DW3 commanders contributed exploration data to make Rainbow's End operational, then faced being declared outlaws before blackmail material forced the superpowers to back down and grant full pardons.
articles.modern_impact: This chapter establishes Rainbow's End as a permanent deep-space installation serving as an inhibitor over a Guardian nexus archive—creating a new frontier outpost with tripartite superpower oversight, while revealing the fragility of political support for existential scientific endeavors.
articles.body_full:
DW 3 Carrier Odysseus, 3312 AD

Jasmina Halsey woke as if surfacing through layers of ice.

At first there was only light. Not the hard clinical light of a med-bay lamp, but a whiteness diffused through half-closed lids, bright enough to ache and yet still distant, as though she were looking at it from the bottom of cold water. Then came sound: the low pulse of shipboard machinery, the soft chatter of a diagnostic unit, the hiss of recycled air moving through vents. Somewhere close by, someone shifted their weight in a chair and tried not to look relieved too quickly.

When she finally opened her eyes properly, Doctor Gery was leaning over her with the careful expression of a man who knew his patient had already outstripped his textbooks.

“Welcome back,” he said. “Though if you disappear into witch-space again, I’d appreciate a little warning next time.”

Jasmina blinked once, slowly, then turned her head. The medbay on the Odysseus was quiet, sealed away from the rest of the carrier’s noise. Beyond the partition she could see the starfield hanging still and indifferent. Closer at hand stood Hermine Delarue, arms folded so tightly she might have been bracing herself against the bulkheads.

“You look dreadful,” Hermine said.

Jasmina’s mouth twitched. “That must mean I’m improving.”

Hermine did not smile. There was too much fatigue in her face for that, too much held in reserve.

“You vanished,” she said flatly. “Your ship was torn apart. We pulled you out of an escape pod that should not have worked and found no sensible explanation for any of it. So before you ask me for anything heroic or inconvenient, I would very much like to know where exactly you’ve been and what the hell you thought you were doing.”

Jasmina closed her eyes briefly. The memory returned all at once — not in fragments, but with the impossible clarity of a thing that had happened outside time and had therefore never had the chance to blur. The Connect. The equations. The voices that were not what she had first assumed, but were in fact the Caretakers themselves. The revelation of the it.

When she looked at Hermine again, there was a steadiness in her that had not been there before.

“The Quirium Unit?” she asked, almost rhetorically.

“Presumed destroyed,” Hermine answered. “At least our salvage teams found no trace of it in the wreckage.”

“I know what the Caretakers are,” Jasmina said abruptly.

Hermine’s expression changed almost imperceptibly, from exasperation to caution.

“Go on.”

“They are not gods. Not ghosts. Not even what we thought they were. They are the remnant intelligences of the species we call the Guardians — or more precisely, the preserved equations of minds their civilisation built to advise, preserve and remember. They live within the lattice. They are the harmony of it. After they went to war with the Thargoids, all that remains is their essence, their code, their… soul.”

Doctor Gery took a discreet step backwards, deciding this was now above his pay grade.

“And?” Hermine asked.

“And there is something else in there with them.” Jasmina pushed herself upright with more ease than she should have possessed. “A rogue human AI. Ancient. Flawed. Mobile. It escaped its creators and has spent centuries learning how to survive in witch-space, how to spread itself through communication and through transit. It has found the old Guardian archive nexus points and is slowly overwriting the lattice itself. That is what the Caretakers have been trying to warn us about — my visions from all those years ago. They couldn’t reach humanity in any other way. Communication is only possible in witch-space… and somehow, I was the only receptive person.”

“This is crazy…”

“Listen to me. The rogue AI is hostile, bitter towards the humanity that created it. It wants to destroy us. Or control, I don’t know. Whether that’s revenge or simply logical implacability, I’m not sure. That is what happened to the Missing. That is what must have happened to the Guinevere. That is what happened to the DSSA carrier and the ancient wrecks. They wandered too close to something that has learned to use witch-space like a bloodstream.”

“Too close?”

“Well, not necessarily by proximity. Maybe in terms of technology. Or not, maybe the opposite… Still, we must go there. We must build the station there.”

That made no sense. Hermine stared at her for a long time.

Then she said, very carefully, “No.”

Jasmina frowned. “No?”

“No, Jasmina. Not ‘no, I don’t believe you’, though let us be honest, that is also very much on the table. No as in absolutely not. I am not redirecting eight thousand commanders and half a logistical chain on the basis of a near-death experience and a conversation you claim to have had with dead machines in hyperspace.” She exhaled sharply through her nose. “Do you have any idea how insane that sounds?”

“Yes,” Jasmina said. “I do. It sounded insane to me when I was in it.”

“Then help me out here.”

Jasmina swung her legs over the side of the bed and stood. There was a moment where the room should have tilted and did not.

“The station,” she said. “The one we planned to build in the Veils. It has to be moved. We can’t build it in the original system. We need its technology elsewhere.”

Hermine’s eyes narrowed.

“No.”

“It has to be built where the nexus vault is. The Mare Somnia.”

“Absolutely not. That’s a few thousand light years off the itinerary.”

“It has to be there, Hermine. The Caretakers were very clear on this. The station, with the GalCop sensor array and the meta-alloy shielding on the Fimbulthul, can function as an inhibitor. A capstone. A dampener on the lattice. It will lock the rogue AI in situ. If we place it over the archive point, we can suppress the rogue AI’s access to the lattice and trap it below the surface where it has rooted itself.”

“And you know this how exactly?”

“They…” she hesitated, aware of the absurdity of it all. “They told me. No, made it clear to me is a better term. Like waking up from a dream and knowing what happened but not how.”

“You are asking me,” Hermine said, each word clipped, “to move a pre-planned deep-space construction project to a secret location you learned from an incorporeal alien intelligence… while you were actually dead.”

“Temporarily dead,” Jasmina said.

Hermine glared at her.

“I need proof, Jasmina,” Hermine said at last. “And yet another incorporeal vision is not enough.”

For a moment the silence in the medbay thickened into something almost visible. It would have curdled into a proper argument had the lights not flickered at exactly that moment.

Every display in the room dimmed. The med monitors dropped to amber. Somewhere deep in the carrier a relay clicked. Then the comms panel above the doorway came to life with a sound none of them recognised — not a carrier ping, not a standard priority hail, but a low chirruping burst that seemed to arrive from nowhere and everywhere at once.

Hermine turned slowly.

“What the heck?”

The panel did not display an origin. No system tag. No relay identifier. No carrier prefix. Just static, and then a voice, heavily compressed and distorted, yet vaguely familiar, speaking through what sounded like half a dozen mismatched codecs.

“Miss Delarue,” it said calmly. “The Mare Somnia. Do what Halsey requires.”

That was all.

The panel went dark.

For the first time since Jasmina had woken, Hermine looked genuinely unsettled.

“Trace that,” she snapped.

Doctor Gery, who had no business being involved in this and yet now clearly was, tapped at the panel and shook his head. “No source. No handshake. No packet path. It just… appeared. And now it’s deleted itself.”

Jasmina said nothing. She didn’t need to. The silence between them did the work for her.

Hermine rubbed a hand over her face. Then, very slowly, she lowered it and looked at Jasmina.

“Proof enough?” Jasmina asked, a faint smile playing on her lips.

“I hate this expedition,” Hermine muttered.

“You really don’t.”

“No,” Hermine admitted. “But I hate this part of it.”

She drew herself up, visibly rearranging irritation into command.

“Fine. We move the build. Quietly. No poetry in the bulletin, no spectral revelations, no ‘the voices in witch-space told us to’. We do this on engineering grounds, scientific necessity and because some untraceable lunatic with impossible comms access has just put a boot through my decision-making process.”

Jasmina smiled faintly. “That will do.”

---
The build itself took on the character of all difficult things in deep space: first impossible, then inevitable.

The logistics detachment altered course under a dozen technical pretexts. Miners fed the carriers. Fabricators ran hot for cycles on end. Construction crews assembled modules in the dark under a sky that offered no encouragement whatsoever. The chosen system lay on the borders of what Bubble astronomers had decided to be the Mare Somnia, the Sea of Dreams; and it lay some thousand light years below the galactic plane, isolated and remote. 

A perfect place to hide and hatch plans. 

It also harboured the hidden vaults under a moon’s blasted surface and whoever used the lattice signature firmware saw the system’s white dwarf shimmering like heat on metal. Witch-space was close.

And now the station…

They built it because there was nothing else to do.

They built it because commanders always preferred work to waiting.

They built it because even fear, if given a welder and a timetable, can make itself useful.

When the station’s skeleton finally locked into place above the designated world, someone on an open channel laughed and asked what they were going to call the thing.

There was a long pause.

Then Jasmina, standing on the observation,  said quietly, “This is literally the end of the rainbow.” She shrugged. “Call her Rainbow’s End.”

No one argued with her.

The name went into the registry. An Ocellus station, constructed not just in the back of beyond, but several light years away from the middle of nowhere and a number of parsecs off the edge of the map.

---
The final fitting-out was where the theory turned dangerous.

The old GalCop sensor array from the Fimbulthul was stripped and remounted into the station’s central spine. The prototype Meta-alloy radiation shielding from the science carrier’s protected compartments was fitted around the relevant systems in overlapping bands and realigned, not because anyone fully understood how it would work, but because Ram Tah’s models, Lya’s equations and Jasmina’s impossible testimony all pointed in the same direction. The alien alloys had an effect on the lattice.

An inhibitor.

Not a weapon.

Not a cure.

A cap.

A lid placed carefully over a hole no one wanted to look into for too long.

To make the station truly operational, Hermine insisted on one more layer of reason.

“If we’re going to commit this act of engineering blasphemy,” she said, “then the station is going to function as a station. Feed it data. Properly. Make it useful. We need plausible cover anyway.”

And so the call went out.

Exploration data. Fresh survey models. Stellar scans. Planetary profiles. Anything the commanders had gathered in the surrounding volume.

They responded in force.

Data poured into Rainbow’s End until its databanks swelled with the weight of the nearby unknown. Modellers cursed, then adapted. Analysts stopped sleeping. The station became, by degrees, real.

And then, when the final systems came online and the inhibitor engaged, the lattice shifted. Not violently, not theatrically. There was no flare, no wave of distortion, no chorus in the comms.

Just a measurable weakening.

The fifteen-cycle miss softened. The pressure in the lattice signatures dipped. The ugly overtones that had clung to the region for so long receded like an infection finding itself walled off from the bloodstream.

Lya’s face appeared by telepresence, pale from lack of sleep and lit by equations.

“Gosh! I think it worked,” she said, almost disbelieving. “I don’t know precisely how it worked, which I hate, but it worked.”

Hermine stood very still in the station’s central control room, arms folded as always.

“For now,” she said.

“For now,” Jasmina agreed. The unpleasant subconscious echo that had travelled in her mind all the way from the core worlds was somehow placated now, easier, more relaxed.

Hermine let out a breath that might almost have been relief.

“Then we continue according to plan. Fully survey the system, chart everything, establish proper buffers and handoff procedures.”

Jasmina shook her head.

“No. DW3 moves on.”

Hermine looked at her sharply. “What?”

“The situation is contained, not ended. The station can sit. Deep Space Surveys and maybe later the DSSA can watch it. The rest…” She glanced at the white dwarf in the distance. “The rest belongs to others now.”

Hermine studied her for a long moment, then nodded once.

“Fine. We move.”

---
It should have ended there. Naturally it didn’t.

Instead, the news leaked.

Not through official channels. Not in any clean way anyone could track. But within days the Bubble was thick with fragments: an ancient rogue AI in witch-space here, a hidden nexus archive there, a deep-space station built over… something… something that should not exist, a machine consciousness held at bay by alien tech and desperate improvisation. It was a mess, and apparently a calculated one. 

It hit all three superpowers like a collision warning. A summit was convened, ironically about ‘unforeseen opportunities of technological exchanges’. Federation, Empire, Alliance. And Aegis.

The three superpowers never agreed on anything important, yet there was one thing they did have in common. Long ago, sentient AI had been banned by consensus. There had been rumours in previous centuries that some of these might have escaped into deep space. Regor sector was often named in tinfoil circles. The revelation that one had somehow survived and was now embedded in some kind of galaxy-spanning latticework with likely hostile intentions was unsettling in the extreme.

This time there was no polite ambiguity. Orders went out.

Distant Worlds 3 was to stand down and begin immediate return transit. Rainbow’s End was to be dismantled and, if necessary, destroyed. Officially this was a containment measure. Unofficially everyone on site understood what it meant.

Destroy the inhibitor and whatever lay beneath it would be free again.

The response from the Bubble was short-sighted, fearful and precipitous. Military minds thinking that simply blowing stuff up was a solution in itself.

The order reached the expedition in a hard, cold data packet.

Hermine read it once in silence, then passed it to Jasmina.

Jasmina read it through to the end.

“Well,” she said. “They’ve noticed. I suppose it was ridiculous to assume we could keep a lid on this. They’re ordering us to decommission and return, on pain of being made outcasts. Battlecruisers from all three superpowers are already being prepped.”

“President Winters ordered me as Federal Envoy to make haste,” she added with clear disappointment.

“We better move then,” Hermie mused.

“No,” Jasmina said.

Hermine blinked. “No?”

“No. We do not comply.”

“I just knew you were going to say that…”

That would have been a brave thing to say under any circumstances. Under these circumstances it was near-suicidal.

Within hours the consequences arrived. The speed of FTL comms could be a curse at times: Distant Worlds 3 was vilified. Expedition commanders were reclassified as fugitives. Collective bounties were authorised. The language in the notices was careful, but the meaning wasn’t.

Return. Submit. Or be hunted down and ‘encouraged to retire early’.

The carriers buzzed with anger and disbelief. Pilots who had faced neutron stars and permit locks without complaint now stared at their own governments with open contempt. There were arguments, there was rage, there was fear. Eight thousand commanders suddenly found themselves persona non grata across every civilised world unless they returned immediately and handed themselves and their flight logs in. Bounty hunters were already preparing to cash in, en route to their location, weapons hot, waiting to claim this unexpected bonus. It would be like shooting highly prized fish in a barrel.

---
Alessia Verdi heard the news. She wasn’t all that surprised. She had seen how the superpowers reacted when galactic events took unexpected turns.

She found Jasmina in a side room off the station’s operations deck, looking at the latest bulletin as though she might shame it into becoming less stupid.

“You’ve annoyed three governments at once,” Alessia said. “That takes talent.”

Jasmina looked up. “If you’re here to tell me this was a mistake, get in line.”

“I’m here,” Alessia said, closing the door behind her, “to tell you I know where some of the bones are buried.”

She sat without invitation, all long-practised fatigue and Imperial poise.

“You’ve heard the whispers about Salomé coming back from the dead,” she said. “I told you it was rubbish. I was there when Kahina Tijani Loren died. She died very thoroughly. But in the aftermath…” She held Jasmina’s gaze. “A lot of people did a lot of very dirty things to make sure the story stayed tidy. The Club. The suppressions. The records. The collusion. The Federation, the Empire, the Alliance — all of them have disease and rot in the same bulkheads.”

Jasmina went still.

“And you can prove it?”

Alessia’s smile was thin and tired. She pulled a small commtab from her pocket and flicked it towards Jasmina in the zero-gee. It tumbled innocently through the air. Jasmina caught it.

“Plenty of it,” Alessia replied. “Several terabytes. Enough to break careers. Enough to collapse ministries. Enough to make all three superpowers remember that they prefer the status quo to the actual truth.”

“And what is your price?”

Alessia considered the question.

“Nothing, really,” she said at last. “Except perhaps the satisfaction of reminding them that history has claws. I’ve named the file Salomé’s Requiem. They’ll know they are in trouble immediately when they see that. They’ll back off. If they don’t, release it publicly and watch the fireworks… but trust me, that won’t happen.”

The two women regarded each other for a long moment. 

“I’ll owe you one,” Jasmina said. “We all will.”

“Yes,” Alessia said, with another faint smile. “You will. I may cash that in one day.”

---
The blackmail, if that was the word for it, was conducted with remarkable elegance. The channels were quiet, precise and implied political lethality. Messages were sent, archives hinted at, confirmations implied. Names were invoked with surgical precision.

And, because there were still some adults left in the galaxy, Ambassador Cuthrick Delaney stepped in before the thing became a constitutional bloodbath.

By the time he arrived on the secure tri-power channel he had already done what seasoned diplomats do best: turned panic into process.

The compromise he forged was ugly, sensible and therefore real. Rainbow’s End would remain operational. Deep Space Surveys, as the originators of the whole endeavour,  would maintain it. Federation, Empire and Alliance would each provide observers and supervisory oversight. And of course Universal Cartographics would be allowed to the table as well. After all, it was all about science, wasn’t it?

No one would destroy the station.

No one would admit publicly how close they had come.

And the Distant Worlds commanders would be pardoned in full and allowed to return home without sanction. The orders rescinding the bounties went out twelve hours later.

The fleet, which had spent those twelve hours on the edge of becoming something far more dangerous than an expedition, settled by degrees.

Not calm.

Not trust.

Something more cautious.

Something like a truce.

---
Later, standing on the outer promenade of Rainbow’s End, Jasmina looked out across the station that should not have existed and yet now shone quietly against the darkness.

Below, somewhere beneath the crust of the lattice it watched over, the rogue AI remained trapped or muffled or slowed. Contained, for now, beneath layers of alloy, mathematics and human bloody-mindedness.

The lattice no longer screamed. It only whispered.

Beside her, Hermine folded her arms and regarded the stars with the expression of a woman already working out how much paperwork all this would generate in peacetime.

“Well,” she said eventually, “that was unpleasant.”

Jasmina laughed softly.

“Yes.”

“You know it isn’t over.”

“No,” Jasmina said. “Only paused. Mare Somnia, a waking beacon in a Sea of Dreams. Let’s hope it’ll not turn into our next nightmare.”

Hermine nodded toward the station lights below.

“Still. Not bad for a glorified data depot.”

Jasmina looked at Rainbow’s End — at the name, the lights, the impossible fact of it — and thought of the Caretakers in their fading harmony, of the many ships that had died trying to say the same thing, of the thing below and the thing beyond and the long chain of accidents and choices that had brought them here.

Contained.

Not ended.

For now, that would have to be enough.

For Michael Brookes.

articles.body_full:
October Consortium has confirmed that Radicoida unica, an enigmatic flora found exclusively within HIP 87621, has entered an active reproductive phase.
According to their scientific teams, the plant’s dormant cycle has ended, triggering the growth of hardened ‘seed pods’ across its upper platforms. These pods hold rare biological material believed to be the main source of the species highly valued physiological effects.
Researchers say that this activation validates early theories about the plant’s sensitivity to nearby life signatures, with its bloom phase perceived as a direct response to recent studies by Commanders of the Pilots’ Federation. Sceptics noted that some Radicoida sites are yet to bloom, however.
Military and corporate restrictions are still in effect while oversight of the enclave is coordinated in line with the recent October Accords. October Consortium has therefore called upon Commanders to support a new phase of exobiological harvesting. The collected seed pods will undergo detailed analysis and biochemical synthesis to better understand their unique properties.
Exogene Sciences in HIP 87621 has been authorised as the central collection point for incoming samples, with October Consortium overseeing transfer and storage. Scientists hope this phase of data acquisition will unlock further leaps in the pharmacological applications of Radicoida unica.
Commanders are encouraged to exercise caution, as the plant continues to thrive on worlds with hazardous temperatures and volatile surface conditions.

articles.title: Radicoida Unica Research Initiative Concludes
articles.summary: Radicoida unica in HIP 87621 enters bloom phase producing seed pods. October Consortium calls for harvesting to support pharmacological research. Exogene Sciences is collection point.
articles.player_impact: New CG: collect Radicoida unica seed pods at Exogene Sciences in HIP 87621. Plant entered active reproductive phase. Hazardous surface conditions.
articles.modern_impact: Mass seed pod collection provides October Consortium with unprecedented biological material stockpile. Dr. Casimir's explicit denial of a Ventura connection actually amplifies suspicion by raising the comparison, suggesting the wellness trend and Radicoida research may eventually converge in public consciousness.
articles.body_full:
October Consortium has announced that the research initiative to collect Radicoida unica bloom samples was a resounding success.
According to results reported from Exogene Sciences in HIP 87621, the number of Unica seed pods collected by Commanders has meant that research efforts will be helped significantly due to the increased availability of biological material.
The collected seed pods will now undergo detailed, multi-faceted analysis to further understand their unique properties in the hope of reproducing the pharmacological effects seen in recent studies.
A legal representative at October Consortium added:
“Our research and development projections will be greatly fortified thanks to the thousands of Commanders who took part in this initiative. All members of the October Accords will benefit from this outcome.”
Contributing Commanders can now collect their rewards at Exogene Sciences.
Meanwhile, some reaction pundits have noted similarities between the Holloway Institute’s recent Radicoida study and a viral wellness trend attributed to movie star William Ventura’s self-recorded fitness regime.
Although the timing is curious, Dr. Casimir of the Holloway Bioscience Institute claimed to Vox Galactica that ‘the development time and regulatory framework needed to get Radicoida-based enhancers anywhere close to human trials are some ways away,’ and suggested Big Bill’s physical transformation was down to ‘diet meds and confidence tricks.’

articles.title: Unidentified Mercenary Group Linked to Fabrication Facility Break-In
articles.summary: Break-in at LHS 1167 fabrication plant by disciplined mercenary group with unknown insignia. Well-equipped ships and coordinated tactics suggest organized new faction.
articles.player_impact: New mercenary threat with heavily modified ships and unfamiliar insignia. Bounty hunting opportunities likely as authorities investigate.
articles.modern_impact: Disciplined mercenary group with unfamiliar insignia and modified ships signals the emergence of a non-aligned military force. Theft of fabrication hardware suggests capacity for autonomous ship production, potentially creating a new armed faction independent of superpower or corporate control.
articles.body_full:
Authorities are investigating a break-in at a fabrication plant in the LHS 1167 system, following the theft of hardware and components. 
No group has yet claimed responsibility, but early evidence points toward an unfamiliar mercenary outfit operating across multiple regions of the Bubble.
Security footage recovered from the site shows coordinated ship movements and disciplined withdrawal patterns, prompting speculation that the perpetrators were neither opportunistic pirates nor local criminals. Reports of heavily modified vessels bearing unfamiliar insignia have since surfaced in neighbouring systems.
A spokesperson for the affected facility issued a blunt assessment to Vox Galactica:
“These weren’t amateurs. The ships we encountered were exceptionally well-equipped and flown with precision. They absorbed punishment that would have crippled most raiders.”
Local authorities have advised independent pilots to remain vigilant and report sightings of unusual ship markings or coordinated mercenary activity. While officials stress that there is no immediate threat to civilian populations, analysts suggest the incident may signal the emergence of a new group within the galaxy’s increasingly crowded security landscape.
Further updates will be released as the investigation continues.

articles.title: Ancient Origins Suggested in Radicoida Unica Study
articles.summary: Phylogenetic study of Radicoida unica suggests DNA markers indicating ancient non-natural intervention. October Consortium declines comment. Speculation about deliberate design vs natural evolution.
articles.player_impact: Revelation that Radicoida unica may have ancient engineered origins. No direct gameplay yet but deepens the mystery of HIP 87621 flora.
articles.modern_impact: Engineered DNA markers on an eon timescale raise the possibility of precursor civilization intervention. If connected to Guardians or other ancient species, Radicoida may be part of a distributed biological legacy across the galaxy. October Consortium's silence fuels speculation and may attract independent xenoarchaeological investigation.
articles.body_full:
New analysis of Radicoida unica has raised fresh questions about the true origins of the enigmatic flora found in HIP 87621.
Following the recent seed pod recovery initiative, researchers acting under the October Accords have begun detailed phylogenetic studies using the expanded sample pool.
Early findings suggest that certain evolutionary markers within the plant’s DNA may not be entirely natural.
According to sources close to the project, specific sequences within the seed pods biochemical structure show evidence of non-environmental diversion. However, scientists were quick to stress that such changes were not recent.
One researcher, speaking anonymously, stated that the markers indicate intervention “on a timescale measured in eons rather than millennia,” and theorised that if the plant was engineered, it was “by an unknown agent in the very distant past.”
The implications of such a discovery remain unclear.
Some analysts have speculated that the plant’s unique pharmacological properties may be the result of deliberate design, rather than natural evolution.
Others have urged restraint, noting that exotic evolutionary paths can produce similarly unusual results and there is still so much to learn about this species of flora.
October Consortium representatives declined to comment on the findings, reiterating only that research into Radicoida unica remains ongoing and tightly controlled.

articles.title: Competing Claims Emerge Over Wellness Surge
articles.summary: William 'Big Bill' Ventura's fitness trend evolves into broader cultural movement. Unusually consistent reports of improved wellbeing across professions. No product or organization credited.
articles.player_impact: Social/cultural event with no direct gameplay. Viral wellness trend continues spreading. Monitor for potential commodity or CG implications.
articles.modern_impact: Sirius Corporation's nutrient product claims and Kit Fowler's Onionhead speculation introduce competing explanations for the wellness trend. The persistence of enhanced wellbeing reports without clear attribution suggests either a genuine unexplained phenomenon or a deliberately concealed cause that may eventually surface through investigative reporting.
articles.body_full:
As reports of improved health and mental performance continue across a number of systems, several institutions have begun attributing the trend to their own initiatives.
Health authorities have pointed to recent dietary guidance reforms and public exercise incentives, while corporate voices, including Sirius Corporation, have highlighted advances in nutrient-dense, low-calorie food products for mainstream markets.
Marketing analysts note a sharp rise in campaigns emphasising “optimised living” and “holistic performance,” though no single product dominates the conversation. “Big Bill” Ventura, the actor whose viral workout series inspired the trend, has recently signed several lucrative sponsorship deals.
Amid the consensus-building, familiar dissent has surfaced. Kit Fowler, a long-time conspiracy commentator, questioned the suddenness of the shift during a recent episode of the End Times broadcast:
“People don’t just wake up feeling this good,” Fowler claimed.
“Either something’s being added to the supply chain, or something’s being left out of the conversation.”
Fowler went on to speculate about unregulated performance enhancers, possibly linked to a new strain of Onionhead, though provided no evidence. His remarks have been widely dismissed by officials yet continue to circulate among fringe networks.
Authorities stress there is no cause for concern and encourage citizens to rely on verified information as analysis of the fitness trend continues.

articles.title: Coordinated Raids Hit Outposts Across Core Systems
locations: Several military ports across the core
articles.summary: Military outposts across the Bubble hit by coordinated raids. Twin-axe malware signature suggests a rogue pirate strategist uniting ships under one banner. Trade associations warn of falling confidence.
articles.player_impact: New organized pirate threat with twin-axe malware calling card. Coordinated raids on military outposts across core systems. No faction claims responsibility yet.
articles.modern_impact: Twin-axe malware signature and coordinated military-port raids indicate an organized pirate coalition with technical sophistication matching some military forces. A rogue strategist uniting ships under one banner mirrors the power-coalition dynamics seen in HIP 87621, suggesting decentralized authority structures may become a recurring threat model.
articles.body_full:
Several military ports across the core systems have been targeted in a wave of raids this week, according to Vox Galactica.
While no structural damage was reported at any of the raid locations, system authorities confirmed that military supplies were stolen and security personnel were briefly overwhelmed during the attacks.
In several cases, investigators noted that the raids followed a coordinated pattern rather than the opportunistic strikes usually associated with piracy, prompting concerns over organised criminal activity in systems typically considered secure.
Crime correspondent Mira Bukowski writes:
“While no single faction has issued a statement to claim responsibility for the attacks, underground sources claim a rogue pirate strategist has united a coalition of pirate ships under one banner. Digital malware displaying a twin axe motif disrupted security networks during the raids, believed to be a calling card of this individual.”
Trade associations have raised the issue with local governments, warning that confidence among market operators could fall if the perpetrators are not dealt with swiftly.
For now, the affected outposts are still operating as normal. But the pattern of the attacks has left many wondering whether a more serious threat may be growing in the shadows.

articles.body_full:
After having spent a month in the Trojan Belt and Arcadian Stream, the Distant Worlds Expedition has again entered regions with higher stellar density.
The flotilla is now bound for Waypoint 13 in its epic jaunt. Expedition Command confirmed their scientific projects around stellar density and properties surveys were still ongoing.
“Ever since we left Rainbow’s End, we have conducted dozens of sector sweeps,” DSS Operations Executive Hermine Delarue confirmed. “The data models we could prepare at Rainbow’s End with so many Commanders’ exploration data really paid off and now facilitate many of our daily scans.”
Delarue confirmed the expedition flag carrier, Odysseus, will install a special commemorative beacon in the waypoint system which, on scanning it, will register any Commander’s callsign and store it in a data vault for later laurels.
Chief Astronomer Lynda Amanda ter Holt also confirmed the flotilla will take the opportunity to visit the nearby Guardian ruins in the Teal Nebula, formally catalogued as Eorl Auwsy AA-A H72:
“To the best of our knowledge, the Guardian ruins in the Teal Nebula may be the least explored, because they are quite remote. So why not take a look while we’re around? I bet Ram Tah is watching us with envy right now.”
After another three days full of exploration revelry, the expedition will once again prepare for their next leg of the journey, of which there will be a successive report in due time.

Reports indicate that criminal elements remain active in the system. Authorities have requested that independent combat pilots help to eliminate this hostile presence while rescue operations can be completed.
A spokesperson for Lhou Mans system security added:
“We’ve been given no motive for the attacks and the situation remains serious. Help is needed to evacuate those still trapped and ensure all hostiles are driven out of the system.”
Pilots willing to assist should register immediately at Ryman Enterprise in Lhou Mans.
