articles.title: You Know Now
articles.author: Andrew Gaspurr
articles.summary: Weeks after leaving Rainbow's End, Halsey and Hermine discuss whether the containment will hold. Halsey visits Guardian ruins in the Teal Nebula with Nadya Holdstock. The obelisks react to her presence, flashing in sequence as she passes—an honour guard acknowledging her attunement to the Connect. In her mind she senses the Guardian entity: "You know now. You have purpose. Now do." Meanwhile, Hermine meets Cynthia Sideris of Universal Cartographics, who reveals PF-registered firmware irregularities in DW3 ships and offers Hermine an Executive Director position in exchange for the modified firmware and debriefing.
articles.player_impact: The expedition's modified firmware—designed to detect lattice anomalies—attracted attention from the Pilots' Federation and Universal Cartographics, affecting all pilots who uploaded the patch. The Guardian obelisks' reaction to Halsey confirmed a living connection between human consciousness and the ancient network.
articles.modern_impact: The final chapter establishes that the conflict between corporate interests, superpower politics, and the Guardian/AI lattice is far from resolved. Halsey's new purpose and the offer to Hermine suggest the next phase will play out in the corridors of power rather than deep space.
articles.body_full:
Eorl Auwsy SY-Z d13-450, 3312 AD

Jasmina Halsey stood in front of the crystal window in the Odysseus’ starboard observation lounge, immersed and nearly motionless, consuming the blackness beyond with her eyes.

And possibly with her soul, Hermine Delarue thought.

She had entered the lounge silently and noticed the subtle trembling in Jasmina’s left hand. It had started shortly after they left Rainbow’s End a few weeks ago. And ever since she had found her in the observation lounge, standing there for hours, trying to sense the cosmos.

“Anything?” Hermine asked.

Jasmina’s answer came an eternity later: “No. Nothing.”

Hermine moved a few steps closer but said nothing.

“Maybe we should have stayed a few days longer. We should have made sure everything was in order. I mean we didn’t even bother to double check on the systems we installed at Rainbow’s End. The Galcop array, the shielding…”

She slowly turned around, a mixture between doubt and despair written all over her face.

“What if it didn’t last?”

Hermine considered that for a moment.

“You insisted we leave immediately after we filled Rainbow’s memory buffers with all that exploration data. We made sure our lattice signature was buried under petabytes of stellar surveys. Uninitiated station crew will not be able to find it. It’s as secure as we could make it given the circumstances.”

“I know,” Jasmina replied. “Still, I would have wished for a confirmation from our Guardian friend that everything was in order. A thank you, if you want to put it that way.”

“Jas, did you really think a million year old non-human AI who probably has seen a few stars explode and lives in hyperspace would say so long and thanks for all the fish?”

“Yes,” she shrugged. “Except for the fish maybe.”

Then, smiling a wry smile, she added: “Call me too human but I think we here, all of us, deserve a thanks. And I thought… I thought when not even our own species has the guts to thank us for all the pain, the hardship and all this space madness, would it be too much for the thing we actually rescued to say okay, nicely done?”

Hermine stared at her for a long moment.

“Well, would it?”

“That’s your job, Jas.”

“What?!”

Hermine remained calm, crossing her arms. “It’s your job. Simple as that. You are the Federal Envoy tasked to oversee an investigation, remember? You may be the AI’s pen friend but your real duty is being a Federal Envoy to the expedition. And to me as a rep of DSS.”

“Are you serious?” 

“I sure am. Staring into the void solves nothing. Neither does hoping you won a friend for life with this one. We need to figure out what all this really means. The wrecks, the matter manipulation, the AI in hyperspace, radio messages hundreds of years old, the myths about the Archer’s Shadow, implications for exploration… What does all this mean for us mortals reaching for the stars?”

“Poetic… You mean what can we actually tell them?”

“Well, for starters, you need to say thanks to all the explorers out there. You of all people. At times we have been honest with them and at times we have been gaslighting them. There is no way to frame it differently and were Lya here she would start babbling about her Snark hunting poem again, I guess.”

Jasmina couldn’t do much more than look at Hermine, doubt slowly making way to more important things like duty and responsibility. They slowly flooded back into her beleaguered mind. 

“Reality catches up with us, Jas. You need to make room for your species again. And you have the obligation to address them and their concerns,” she added. “You cannot assume that AI acts on human scales when it comes to morality and politeness. But all those explorers do.”

“I haven’t heard a voice in my head for weeks now!” Jasmina insisted, her hand still trembling. She made a fist.

“Well, what did you expect? We buried it. And besides, most humans would consider not hearing voices in their heads a good thing.”

“Very well…”

Hermine took another step towards her, resting her hands gently on her shoulders.

“I am here for you, whenever you want to talk. But soon we’ll be nearing the Bubble again and quite frankly, we need your savvy and political acumen to sail those waters. Yes, we have been cleared but only through out-scheming the schemers.”

“Did you erase our records then?” Jasmina suddenly asked. “Flight logs, evac plans, neutron scans, all that goofy stuff? We cannot risk another leak making 8,000 explorers outcasts again. We used up nearly all our clout dealing with the last one and yes, I’m not even sure we’re welcome back home.”

“We aren’t,” Hermine conceded. “Not us decision makers anyway. They’ll give us a standing ovation and some photo ops when we return, praise all our achievements ‘for all mankind’ and how we made history again. But in their minds they will never forget how we blackmailed ourselves back into their good graces.” 

She sighed.

“Have you heard anything from our two elderly gentlemen?” Jasmina asked.

“Nope. Ermitage left a voice message saying he still had to deal with a few contacts of his and from Cal there’s been radio silence since we last spoke and he essentially told me we had no business being where we were.” 

“What do you make of this?”

Hermine weighed her head for a good few moments.

“I think it’s possible that covering up whatever Ram Tah has been up to with his AI experiments may be more difficult than they anticipated. And to be honest, Ermitage was never really involved in the day-to-day operations of this expedition. He entrusted DSS with that and although he is kind of an enigmatic person I think he has been as honest as he could be with us.”

“And Cal?”

She shrugged. “Cal is Cal. There is just no knowing what he pulled or what he was able to pull behind the scenes. During the brief talks and sparring matches we had he always kept his guards up while trying to bring mine down, which I admire in a way.”

“But…?”

“But I can’t shake the feeling we haven’t heard the last from him. He has an agenda and I think he used us. For what I don’t know but I can guess it won’t be a small favour he will inevitably ask.”

“I think both have an agenda, and quite possibly they don’t always align.”

“Well, on that we can agree,” Hermine smiled.

“Any last suggestions then before we leave this place and I begin playing politician again and go to the Odysseus’ hairdresser?”

“Yes, we should take a final look at those Guardian ruins in the Teal Nebula,” Hermine proposed. “Apparently Lya and Nadya had a chat about more data for modelling and those ruins down there are far less explored than the ones near the Bubble.”

“Lya and Nadya?”

“Yes. Although I think it’s just Lya wanting to impress Ram Tah with her stuff. I think she has a crush on him.”

“Well,” Jasmina shrugged. “Not all was bad then during our trip.”

“No, not all,” Hermine smiled broadly. “Shall I get your boots on the ground then?”

“Yes, tell Haddard to ready a ship and an SRV for me.”

“Not necessary. Nadya will take you for a ride. She said she has an SRV bay on her Asp so there you go.”

“Holdstock?” Jasmina winced. “That’s just brilliant, thank you so much…”

---
The Scarab made its way past the rows of ancient Guardian obelisks, head lights piercing the darkness. Jasmina had never been to a Guardian site before. Sure, all those reports she had consumed when the ruins had first been discovered but nothing compared to driving through a field of accurately placed silent watchers, tombstones or memorials that may or may not hold the secrets to the Guardians’ ultimate fate.

‘You were the Architects of Creation,’ Jasmina thought. ‘Why did you destroy yourselves?’

There were other tracks in the ruins of course. Many pilots had been eager to get their boots and tyres on the ground, because space madness and all. And Lya was right: These Guardian ruins were far less explored than the scattered locations in the Bubble. 

But right now she was alone, at least on the ground. She had ordered Hermine to assign her a time window without any other pilots around. They were all off to one of Alec’s races or something. Holdstock was still there, however. She had asked — no, insisted — to monitor the ride from low orbit in her Asp. At least they agreed the ruins were the last waypoint where they could reasonably find out if the euphemistically named ‘AI situation’ was contained. If the voices were really silent. 

If she was… alone again?

Her left hand began to tremble, the hand that had so often held the Quirium Control Unit.

‘So many things you could have taught us… So many lessons you learned… Mistakes, insights, your wisdom, your visions, your… love and care for the cosmos…’

Jasmina’s last ride in an SRV had been ages ago. A few visits on sponsored races, ground force training camps and in select R&D facilities as Federation President. And she also remembered one or two test drives in what could have become a prestigious ground based CQC but which was ultimately shelved because the cash was needed for augmenting the navy. 

One of the few things she had agreed on with Hudson back in the day.  

“Halsey,” Nadya called through the SRV intercom, interrupting her past memories. “Did you notice the obelisks?”

Perplexed by the sudden intrusion she looked around, seeing nothing but black silhouettes against the starlight. A city of standing stones. 

“No? What of it?”

“It seems the obelisks react to your presence. There seems to be a pattern.”

“How so?”

“You need to see for yourself,” Nadya answered. “Turn around and drive your Scarab back to the last perimeter point through that row of obelisks. I will take visual footage and relay it to you through your vehicle’s neurolink.”

“Why?”

“Not why. Just do it.”

“Okay?”

Startled by Nadya’s insistence, Jasmina turned the Scarab around. There was no point in debating with this woman. Why was she one of the few people who could get under her skin? She barely even knew her.

She drove back the way she came with the rows of obelisks left and right. When she reached the perimeter point where she started she activated her neurolink and went into remote observation mode.

“Now what?”

“I will send you the footage I made. And then delete it. So see for yourself.”

And what Jasmina Halsey saw was jaw dropping: 

From the bird's view she saw her SRV turning around and driving towards the perimeter point. As she saw her SRV passing the rows of obelisks, they reacted on either side, one by one, flashing in their signature turquoise colour for several seconds as mysterious symbols cascaded from top to bottom before going dark again.

“Halsey…”

An honour guard? An acknowledgement?

“Yes. I see it.”

She closed her eyes but the vision didn’t vanish. The neurolink felt warm and in her mind Jasmina Halsey saw it all in the blink of an eye: The obelisks in rhythm, not just here, but across the Milky Way, humming to a singular tune. The ruins were civilisation, on the surface of living orbs, the dust were people, the rocks were towers, reaching into the heavens and into the Connect… it was everywhere. 

And after a small eternity she finally sensed the entity in the Connect that had spoken to her all this time.

You know now. You have purpose. Now do.

---
In another universe, the universe of corporations, bureaucracy, dealmaking and backstabbing, Hermine Delarue found herself in a telepresence meeting with none other than Cynthia Sideris, Chairwoman of Universal Cartographics. She had even requested a visual broadcast. And said she would pay for it.

“Delly! How good it is to see you.”

The telepresence projector made Sideris sit on a couch, legs crossed, formal dress and holding a porcelain cup. She even smiled somewhat. She had perfected staged appearances long ago.

“Cynthia,” Hermine observed coolly. “Long time no see.”

 “Oh indeed. We must amend that, dear. I hear you will direct your entourage towards civilised space again in the near future. Do you already have any plans for June?”

“I guess I’ll just find my office desks full of paperwork and lecture requests.”

“Splendid! If you want an escape plan, I would invite you to Eridani, maybe have a chat about your findings out there in the wild. ExoCart tells me you even found a big derelict carrier from the DSSA guys and brought it to life again. Wow! You do have some ingenious people out there. I bet their inboxes will be full of job offers once they’re back home.”

“Better job than jail, no?”

“Delly,” Sideris protested, feigning indignance. “I hope you’re not suggesting Universal Cartographics had their hands in this unfortunate misunderstanding? We don’t deal in political amateurism. In fact we made it clear we were fully supportive of your little adventure and would welcome any major uploads to our overflowing databases.”

“I don’t care, Cynthia. And stop this Delly nonsense. What are you, twelve? Yes, we found a DSSA carrier inconveniently stranded uncomfortably close to one of your permit locked sectors.”

Hermine added a shrug: “But you know that, don’t you? You just don’t know yet if we were able to find your Arthurian legend. So stop the charade and let’s get to business, shall we?”

Without so much as a blink or wasting another second the cheerleader was the chairwoman again.

“Very good. So what did you find out?”

“You mean apart from the fact the ship is Eridanus class, built for extended surveys and lab ops and relying on a cryo crew rotation?”

“Yes, exactly.”

“Nothing. Apparently the active crew threw some shanties at Jaques Station, uploaded some of their survey data, probably as payment for their cocktails, and then went off into the unknown.” 

“Hermine,” Sideris shook her head with fake disappointment. “We both know this is not the full story. Bar stories never start or end this way.”

“Enlighten me then. You seem to be better acquainted with bars than I am.”

“Before you so valiantly rescued the DSSA carrier you directed your followers to Rendezvous Point. And interestingly, you seem to have surveyed quite a few K-type stars…”

“And?”

“And? Nothing. It’s just that I think you’re not completely honest with me… with the assignment you were given, specifically asking you to look for the Guinevere.”

“Why K-type stars?” Hermine asked.

“Why not? They are the most promising stars for evolved planetary systems with the biggest habitable zones.”

“So they were looking for habitable worlds?”

“Yes, dear. It’s what survey missions do. Your Distant Things is a prime example. Don’t you even have an Earth 2.0 project or something? Ridiculous.”

“Then why have a cryogenic crew when there really is no need for them in the 3300s anymore? Why have sleepers onboard? It vaguely sounds familiar, I just can’t place it…”

“Internal procedures, dear. I couldn’t possibly comment on that, because it could give our competitors valuable project insights.”

“UniCart doesn’t have competitors.”

Sideris just smiled, her face having turned into a fox having found the henhouse.

“I don’t think it was just goldilocks zones you were after, Cynthia. You could easily buy that data. So it must be something you couldn’t publicly acknowledge you were doing.”

“Sill, no comment but spoiler alert: It’s getting warmer,” Sideris smiled.

“Well,” Hermine said. “I remember one of your rare public statements. Maybe it was a slip of the tongue back then but knowing you a little, I doubt it very much.”

“And what was that?”

“Well, in ‘02 you didn’t rule out aliens on our doorstep. Shortly after Distant Worlds One returned home and while Halsey was looking for her Architects of Creation you said some form of non-human sentience exists in our galaxy.”

“No, I said chances are that some form of non-human sentience exists in our galaxy. If you’re going to quote me, do it right.”

“Still, your comment struck me as odd back in the day. A bit too esoteric for the chairwoman of a megacorporation dealing with buying factual data. And in light of the discovery of the Guardian ruins just a few weeks later I just have to assume there was a PR clockwork ticking. Or maybe you already knew and needed a free of charge follow-up? A community goal, perhaps?”

“Only a fool would discard the notion of us being alone in this big galaxy. And what can I say? It turned out to be true, didn’t it?”

“What was the Guinevere doing out there? You don’t send out exploration cruisers with cryo crews on a whim. And why did we find the DSSA carrier near a permit locked sector? Were they looking for the Guardians?”

“Well, we kindly asked you to find out, didn’t we? But sadly, you seem to have failed in uncovering their whereabouts.”  

“So maybe they took all their secrets with them?”

“No Hermine. Quite the contrary. The plan still is to un-secret the secrets, so to speak. You see, I didn’t ask for this meeting just to show you my porcelain cup. I am going to make you an offer, and I’m only going to do it once. Because offers like these only come once in a lifetime.”

“Depends on how long you live,” Hermine muttered to herself.

“I recently spoke with Zanetti. He said the Pilots’ Federation Safety Board had registered certain ‘irregularities’ in some of your explorers’ ships firmware. Seems like someone inserted some datamining worms looking for extraordinarily exotic data. Something with spacetime and superdense masses?” 

The fox had just turned into a shark.

“I can’t remember all the details but it seems a very explorer thing to do?”  

Then Sideris put on her ‘I’m so sorry’ look. 

“I don’t think I need to point out that tampering with PF firmware is, shall we say, heavily frowned upon?”

Hermine decided to take it in strides. This was cleverly orchestrated and you best dealt with this kind of stunts level headed. Sideris alone was dangerous…

“The flotilla was exonerated by the three Powers, Cynthia. I am not too fussed or even, shall we say, intimidated by a mapping company that can’t even track their own vessels in charted space. You asked DSS to investigate while en route and this is what we did.” 

She made a short pause to let the slight sink in. Level headed, remember?

“If for some reason some of our independent entrepreneurs became creative in using their sophisticated onboard systems you can hardly blame an entire expedition for breaching the 23rd Amendment of the 3187 FTL Safety Act.”

“No, no. Of course not,” Sideris mused. “I am so relieved we are on the same page here and in fact this is entirely not why I am spending millions calling you face to face.”

“What then, Cynthia?” Hermine asked with an artificial sigh. “What are you spending your pocket money on?”

The projector made Sideris put aside her porcelain cup and lean forward on her couch.

“Like I said, I spoke with Zanetti and he put in a good word for you with the Board. So I am authorised to offer you a position within Universal Cartographics with a strong liaison to the PF. You would be Executive Director of a new department focusing on extreme range exploration. One of the key tasks would be to improve and innovate our technological capabilities in that field. It will become more and more important in the future to retain our corporate edge over rather uncoordinated civilian efforts.”

“Something you should be well acquainted with by cleverly manipulating your gone-rogue exploration amateurs,” she added with a (slight) glee.

“And of course,” Hermine concluded, “a few samples of that modified firmware and a debriefing on what we found out there would be beneficial for my nomination.”

Sideris’s smile just could not find an end.

articles.title: Dodec Station Enters Full Production Availability
articles.summary: Brewer Corporation has announced that the Dodec Station has entered full production availability. Previously limited in supply, the Dodec is the largest Tier 3 starport available for colonisation efforts and features three truss variations and an integrated Human Tech Broker.
articles.player_impact: Pilots can now purchase the Dodec Station through any Colonisation contact, allowing them to establish the largest and most capable Tier 3 starport in newly colonised systems.
articles.modern_impact: The full production availability of the Dodec Station significantly expands colonisation infrastructure options for independent pilots, representing the maturation of Brewer Corporation's station construction program and enabling more permanent settlements on the galactic frontier.
articles.body_full:
Brewer Corporation has confirmed that the Dodec Station has entered full production.
Previously available in limited numbers, the Dodec is the largest Tier 3 starport that can be constructed for use in colonisation efforts.
Brewer Corporation CEO Madelyn Teague issued the following statement to Vox Galactica:
"The Dodec is the pinnacle of modern station design. Available with three truss variations and immediate access to a Human Tech Broker, it's simply the best option available for those looking to colonise new systems and to offer services to all who visit."
The Dodec is now widely available for purchase through Colonisation contacts.

articles.title: Criminal Factions Remains Silent After Lhou Mans Attacks
articles.summary: Investigations into the Lhou Mans starport attacks reveal evidence linking the coordinated strikes to a criminal syndicate directed by the rogue pirate admiral known as 'Lady Zi'. The attacks bear similarities to earlier coordinated strikes on military installations in the core systems.
articles.player_impact: Independent pilots assisted with evacuation efforts in Lhou Mans following the attacks. Investigators warn that the system may have been selected for reasons beyond simple disruption, suggesting future combat operations against Lady Zi's coalition fleet may be required.
articles.modern_impact: The emergence of Lady Zi as a coordinated criminal threat in the core systems signals a significant escalation in organised piracy, with potential implications for regional security and the rise of a new major syndicate.
articles.body_full:
Questions remain unanswered following last week’s unprovoked attacks on starport facilities across Lhou Mans.
Security analysts stated that the attacks bore remarkable similarities to last month’s coordinated attacks across military installations in the core systems.
“These patterns are usually reserved for military trials and reconnaissance operations,” a senior security observer told Vox Galactica.
“Simulated attacks are used to probe response times, defensive weak points and the speed with which system security can coordinate with independent pilots.”
Similar data malware packages bearing the hallmarks of twin axe motifs have also been witnessed across Lhou Mans networks.
Crime correspondent Mira Bukowski has revealed evidence from underworld sources allegedly linking the motif to a rogue pirate admiral going by the nom de guerre ‘Lady Zi’ and a coalition fleet directed by a single criminal syndicate.
“Very few are willing to share more details on who Lady Zi is. We don’t know if this is because they are unaware, or if they’re simply scared,” she added.
With evacuation efforts still under way, the attackers’ true motives remain unclear for now. Yet investigators warn that Lhou Mans may have been selected for reasons beyond simple disruption.

articles.title: Civilians Evacuated Safely as Criminal Attacks Defeated
articles.summary: Security forces and independent pilots successfully repelled a coalition of pirate ships in Lhou Mans, completing the civilian evacuation. Defence forces drove out the criminals, but analysts warn this was likely a probing 'test run' for larger coordinated attacks directed by the rogue pirate admiral Lady Zi.
articles.player_impact: Independent combat pilots defended rescue efforts and helped defeat the remaining criminals in Lhou Mans. Pilots are now called to aid starport repair efforts by registering at Ryman Enterprise.
articles.modern_impact: The Lhou Mans attacks confirm Lady Zi as a serious escalating threat in the core systems, with coordinated criminal activities surpassing anything previously experienced. The twin-axe malware signature and probing tactics suggest a highly organised, military-style pirate coalition with ambitions beyond simple piracy.
articles.body_full:
Security forces and independent combat pilots successfully protected rescue efforts after the recent attacks in Lhou Mans.
An alleged coalition of pirate ships hit starports across the system, triggering the evacuation of civilians to safer locations.
Defence forces managed to defeat and drive out the remaining criminals leaving many to wonder what to expect next from Lady Zi. However, analysts are now confident that all signs are pointing towards larger and bolder coordinated criminal activities than have previously been experienced in the past.
“The leading theory is that this was a ‘test run’ of sorts, probing system and port defences in this area of space,” Mira Bukowski wrote for Vox Galactica. “What the next phase of this plan could entail is a source of concern for local authorities.”
Meanwhile, a Zorgon Peterson spokesperson remarked that the new Lynx Highliner performed better than expected under the extreme circumstances.
Engineers monitoring the vessels internal data also showed that the new Mk II cabins outperformed previous cabin modules for comfort even under the most testing of conditions.
With the safe evacuation deemed a success and the new Highliner now available for full distribution across core systems, attention has now turned to repairing the starports damaged in the attack.
Lhou Mans authorities are calling to aid repair efforts and interested pilots should register at Ryman Enterprise.

articles.title: Jaques Station Celebrates Tenth Anniversary of Historic Jump
articles.summary: Jaques Station marks ten years since its historic misjump to the Colonia region. Jaques hints at upcoming celebrations that will have a lasting impact on the frontier colony.
articles.player_impact: Pilots can anticipate upcoming community events tied to Colonia's tenth anniversary celebrations.
articles.modern_impact: Colonia has grown from an accidental settlement into a thriving deep-space civilization. The anniversary highlights how a single station's misjump reshaped humanity's frontier expansion.
articles.body_full:
Today marks the tenth anniversary of the Jaques Station's historic jump that eventually led to the founding of Colonia.
Following a successful community drive to supply the Orbis starport with fuel the week before, the station departed for its intended journey to Beagle Point. However, due to Thargoid sensor interference, it emerged from hyperspace in the Eol Prou RS-T d3-94 system. This system later became known as Colonia.
Jaques, the cyborg bartender and owner of the starport, recalled that event with Vox Galactica:
"I remember that day so vividly! A wildly ambitious endeavour at the time, too. It's hard to imagine ever doing that again."
"Ten years later and Jaques Station is still open, still serving drinks and still selling my famous Jaques Quinentian Still to potent potable enthusiasts. Most importantly, Colonia is thriving. It's high time we celebrated this, I'd say!"
When pressed for more information Jaques simply replied "Soon" with a cybernetic wink, and hinted that the intended celebrations to mark Colonia's tenth anniversary would have a lasting impact should plan go well.
Vox Galactica will be in regular contact with Jaques and the Colonia Council and provide updates ahead of this auspicious occasion.

articles.title: Nadya
articles.author: Andrew Gaspurr
articles.summary: After the expedition's return to the Orion Bubble, Nadya Holdstock packs her gear to depart. She and John Ermitage, the Founder, discuss unresolved matters — the leak, the Three Powers summit allowing Aegis access, and Hewley Jackman's knowledge of Quirium drives from a Sadr Region station. Nadya plans to abandon her current persona and assume a new identity. Ermitage reveals he too will not return to stasis, intending to visit an old companion one last time before stepping away from his role entirely.
articles.player_impact: The conversation reveals that expedition support personnel handled sensitive matters invisible to ordinary pilots — leaks, ancient technology, and superpower politics. Nadya's ongoing investigation into Jackman's Quirium knowledge suggests the expedition uncovered secrets that continue to matter for all pilots travelling in deep space.
articles.modern_impact: The article frames Distant Worlds 3 as one chapter in a much longer saga of secret-keeping spanning decades. Ermitage's decision to abandon his Founder identity and Nadya's need to rotate personas show that the expedition's true architects are moving on, leaving unresolved mysteries — Quirium drives, the Sadr station, and Cal's agenda — for others to confront.
articles.body_full:
Distant Worlds 3 HQ, 3312 AD

She had started packing the moment they arrived in the Orion Bubble and the expedition was over. Her Asp was already on standby and her blue overall and her service cap lay neatly folded on her bunk.

"Leaving us so soon, are you?" she heard that familiar, old voice behind her.

She turned around while binding her ponytail into a short knot.

"There is still the matter of the leak," she insisted. "And the fact Aegis was allowed to the Three Powers summit. I find it concerning, John. Concerning enough to investigate."

"So Nadya is not heading back for Serebrov?"

"No. Apart from the leak and the summit there is still the matter with the Sadr Region."

"And what is that?" John asked.

"It struck me as odd that Hewley Jackman knew about Quirium drives as well; at least superficially. When we investigated the prototype drive of the DSSA Carrier he said he had seen something similar in what he called a 'lone science station in the Sadr region'. I think it is worthwhile to check his background and I intend to inform the Sadr cell."

"I was surprised that anybody knew anything about Quirium at all. GalCop collapsed a long time ago and Falayn went awol. And in Tionisla those control rods are revered as holy artifacts of a bygone age. However, I was not surprised that what little knowledge was left was put into a prototype carrier's hyperdrive. You probably did good to dismantle it when you had the chance. Some secrets deserve to be lost."

She seemed lost in thought for a moment. "I could sense Jacky's anxiousness in that conference and I could not stop pondering. I think he wanted to say more. After all, he always does, but at that moment he refrained."

"That is why I will meet him again," she added. "Although quite likely he will not expect my visit."

He looked at her for a small eternity.

"Very perceptive. And yes, you were always excellent at sensing or reading other people's feelings. It's a gift, really, and you have used it extensively to gain an edge over your assignments. Hell, you even managed to piss off Halsey. That's quite an achievement."

"She is arrogant," she insisted.

He paused.

"You're wrong, Mir. She really isn't. She's brusque, yes. But she's also wounded by the truth. When we speak about personas, don't forget hers was annihilated by her political adversaries after having miraculously survived a covert assassination attempt. And her survival is owed to what was found during Distant Worlds. That's huge. The truth is she was right from the beginning but was sent to a looney bin for it. People should have listened instead."

"I do not think it is over, John. When we surveyed the Norma Arm ruins, the synchronously emitted light patterns of the obelisks suggested that her connection is still active."

"Mir," he said with a soft smile. "I'm not going back to Serebrov either. I can't. There is only that stasis tank waiting for me and who knows when they will unfreeze me again and tell me the galaxy needs saving."

"It's time," he added.

"Time for what?"

"Time to see an old, trusted companion, and then it's time to go."

She turned away abruptly, starting to casually wrap a needle pistol in a towel and stowed it in her bag along with her other few belongings.

"All the more reason to be on my way then," she insisted.

"As Nadya?"

"That is not an option John. I need to adjust her ID and pick a new persona. Procedure requires it. There will be inevitable inconsistencies if someone starts checking her background and we cannot risk that. A few people already started to take an interest during the expedition."

"Well yes, irritating Halsey may have gained you some sympathy," John laughed.

"That is not who I meant and you know it."

"Yes of course, but allow me some humour for a change. I realize meeting Alessia and Andrew again must have been awkward."

"No, I kept it professional. And so did they, as best as they could. Both of them emphasized they have moved on, whatever that means."

"And you know both of them are lying to themselves."

"Sure, but it was not them either. One day when I went to work on the refueling schedule I found a queue of pilots who wanted to thank me for managing their payload intakes."

"And?"

"It was awkward. They came very close."

"Well, they must have been really confused when they found out you don't shake hands."

"I remember you saying it's dangerous for an Elite to have friends," she said with her back still towards him. "How there is always someone out there trying to get you, how friends are a liability and how someone will always try to use them against you. It was part of my training to not have friends and to utilise these liabilities against our adversaries."

"I was bitter and angry," he softly conceded. "Mostly with myself. There will always be more adversaries than friends, Mir, and I came to realise it's why friends are so important. This expedition showed me the value of camaraderie, but it also made painfully clear that I belong to a time that is over."

"And that is it?" she asked, turning half around again. "You have been there from the beginning, right from the start when the Formidine Rift was only known to a few and only whispered among the foolhardy. Those were your words back then. And now the Founder is leaving behind what he founded?"

"It's a stupid title, given to me by the folks who occasionally unfreeze me and ask equally stupid questions. I never liked that. Yes, I had an idea a long time ago how the galaxy could be a better place but nearly all my high and mighty plans failed. And after a small eternity in torpor in this stasis tank I realised it was all just pretence; a redemption arc for the things I did — the things they made me do."

"What I really founded," he added, "was an egoistical plea for absolution. And there is no glory in that. Nor is there any salvation, pun intended."

He sighed. "I only have one friend left and she rests on bedrock. I need to see her one last time and then the galaxy will have its peace with one ancient anachronism gone."

"There is still the other," Mir mused.

"He has his own demons. And he knows they will eventually catch up with him. There is no need to hunt him down now. And he's possibly one of the few people who will elude you anyway if he so wishes."

"He did indeed. Despite you asking me to shadow him I was not very successful."

"That's not true. I knew the odds but I had to make certain he felt shadowed. It's our way of playing chess."

"He is an apparition," John added. "Very much like I am one. But you, Child, you need to care for the living."

"Care?"

"You'll figure it out." He smiled.

articles.title: Guardian Archive Hints at Ancient Radicoida Parallels
articles.summary: Ram Tah has confirmed Guardian Archive passages describing a substance derived from seed pods used by traditionalist Guardian factions to enhance warriors. The biological schematics bear a strong resemblance to recent resonance imaging of Radicoida unica, suggesting a deliberate ancient connection between the flora and the extinct Guardians.
articles.player_impact: No direct call to action, but the discovery validates long-standing speculation about Radicoida unica's ancient engineered origins. Independent pilots who contributed to earlier research initiatives may see future developments as the October Consortium pursues Guardian artefacts based on leaked information.
articles.modern_impact: The discovery establishes a tangible link between Radicoida unica and the extinct Guardian civilization, raising profound questions about deliberate biological engineering across deep time. The unauthorized leak to the October Consortium highlights ongoing tensions between open scientific inquiry and corporate control of xenoarchaeological discoveries. This may reshape understanding of both the Guardians' biological knowledge and the true purpose of Radicoida unica's unique pharmacological properties.
articles.body_full:
Ram Tah has confirmed the existence of previous mention of what appears to be Radicoida unica in the Guardian Archives.
In a statement issued to Leon Banerjee, science correspondent for Vox Galactica, he revealed that in the weeks since the discovery of the rare flora, he has been re-examining Archive data in the hope it would elicit more information about the plant's past origins.
Ram Tah referenced archive passages describing a "kingdom of blessed roots," alongside accounts of a substance derived from seed pods used by Guardian factions that rejected advanced technology.
"These traditionalist groups appear to have utilised a naturally occurring compound to enhance their warriors prior to battle during their civil wars," he explained.
"While much of the context remains unclear, the descriptions are striking."
Additionally, accompanying diagrams within the recovered data include biological schematics that bear a strong resemblance to recent resonance imaging of Radicoida unica.
"It was unfortunate, however, that a member of my team got way ahead of himself and alerted the October Consortium without permission about my discovery," he added.
"I can only assume this is what prompted their sudden interest in Guardian artefacts. We were willing to share this information, after all."
The implications of this discovery remain uncertain, although many now widely believe it may point to a far older, deliberate connection between the species of flora and the long-extinct Guardians.
articles.body_preview:
Ram Tah has confirmed the existence of previous mention of what appears to be Radicoida unica in the Guardian Archives.
In a statement issued to Leon Banerjee, science correspondent for Vox Galactica, he revealed that in the weeks since the discovery of the rare flora, he has been re-examining Archive data in the hope it would elicit more information about the plant's past origins.
Ram Tah referenced archive passages describing a "kingdom of blessed roots," alongside accounts of a substance deri...

articles.title: New Reports of Criminal Fleet Raise Questions
articles.summary: Multiple sightings of ships bearing unidentified markings have been reported across several systems alongside fresh malware sigils linked to Lady Zi. Crime correspondent Mira Bukowski suggests the incidents are connected, while Frontline Solutions prepares expanded anti-criminal services.
articles.player_impact: No direct call to action yet, but Frontline Solutions has strongly hinted at a formal announcement of expanded services to combat criminal activity in the coming days. Pilots should monitor developments for potential combat or logistical opportunities.
articles.modern_impact: The emergence of multiple distinct malware sigils — twin axes, an animal, and an ornate mask — suggests Lady Zi's coalition is larger and more diverse than previously understood, potentially comprising sub-factions or specialised units. Frontline Solutions' planned expansion signals a growing privatisation of anti-piracy efforts in the core systems.
articles.body_full:
Rumours are spreading across several systems following multiple sightings of ships bearing unidentified markings in formation.
Security officials have more reported instances of malware bearing sigils previously discovered in the Lhou Mans attack appearing at otherwise unconnected locations, often at trading outposts, surface ports, and outlying orbital installations.
Multiple malware sigils have also been reported by system authorities investigating data breaches, described as what appears to be 'twin axes', an 'animal', and an 'ornate mask' across separate incidents.
While no formal link has been established between the motifs, Crime correspondent Mira Bukowski has suggested that their appearance is linked to the reports surrounding the emergence of the pirate figure known as Lady Zi.
"These reports are too coincidental to be random and unconnected," she wrote for Vox Galactica.
Imogen le Ray, CEO of Frontline Solutions, responded to the reports indicating in a statement issued to Bukowski for Vox Galactica that "Frontline is preparing to provide additional services to combat the rise in criminal activity," and strongly hinted at a formal announcement in the coming days.

articles.title: Frontline Solutions Announces Expansion of Services
articles.summary: Frontline Solutions expands its mercenary deployment services to counter rising criminal activity, introducing 'The Runner' vessel for rapid squad transport. A resource initiative has been launched in HIP 58412 to independently construct the new fleet.
articles.player_impact: Pilots are invited to register at Pawelczyk Dock in the HIP 58412 system and deliver aluminium, semiconductors and polymers to support construction of Frontline's new Runner-class vessels. Registered combatants may now be lawfully deployed as mercenaries on behalf of hiring factions to counter dangerous criminal activity.
articles.modern_impact: Frontline Solutions' expansion into dedicated anti-criminal operations and independent ship construction represents a major evolution in private military contracting. By avoiding reliance on external manufacturers, Frontline is positioning itself as a fully vertically integrated defence contractor — a development that could reshape how factions and superpowers respond to organised piracy across the galaxy.
articles.body_full:
Frontline Solutions has declared it intends to expand service processes to meet growing demand.
Security analysts have noted that piracy and mercenary groups have become more coordinated since the Second Thargoid War and recommend new tactics to combat the rise in criminal activity.
To meet these demands, Frontline Solutions is offering 'rapid deployment of mercenary strike teams where they are needed, when they are needed'.
"Frontline remains at the forefront of transporting combat-ready squads to faction-led military engagements" Imogen le Ray, CEO of Frontline Solutions stated in a press release.
"I have negotiated with shareholders to expand our coverage. Mercenaries may now be deployed to counter dangerous criminal activity, with registered combatants lawfully acting on behalf of a hiring faction."
Ahead of an expected spike in demand, Frontline announced the launch of a new vessel, dubbed 'The Runner.' This ship has been designed to rapidly transport mercenary squads and ships to operational locations.
"To avoid relying on an external manufacturer, we are independently constructing our Runners to maintain control of our logistical capabilities.", le Ray added, "To ensure we meet our initial deployment targets, we're requesting help for that final push to reach the planned fleet size."
Pilots are invited to support Frontline Solutions by registering at Pawelczyk Dock in the HIP 58412 system before delivering aluminium, semiconductors and polymers to the local market.

articles.title: Radicoida Unica ‘Cultivated, Not Created’ By Guardians
articles.summary: Ram Tah clarified that Radicoida unica is likely a natural flora cultivated by the Guardians millions of years ago for medicinal purposes, not a product of genetic engineering. Dr. Roy Casimir of the Holloway Bioscience Institute echoed the findings, expressing hope that continued research into the plant's medicinal properties will yield further breakthroughs.
articles.player_impact: No direct call to action for pilots. The scientific revelations may influence future opportunities related to Guardian archaeology or Radicoida unica research in the HIP 87621 enclave.
articles.modern_impact: The confirmation of a Guardian connection to Radicoida unica deepens the mystery of the extinct civilization and suggests significant potential for medical breakthroughs. However, the October Consortium's control over the research data raises ongoing concerns about corporate restriction of knowledge that could benefit all humanity.
articles.body_full:
Interest continues to grow among the scientific community following Ram Tah’s speculation that the Guardians once cultivated Radicoida unica for their own use.
With many leading exobiologists continuing to argue over whether Radicoida unica is a direct creation of the Guardians, Ram Tah clarified that the plant is almost certainly a natural flora.
Speaking to Leon Banerjee, science correspondent for Vox Galactica, Tah reiterated that whilst the context in the Guardian Archive links the long extinct race to using the plant, there is no evidence it was a creation of genetic engineering.
"There is evidence that the Guardians cultivated the plant for their own purposes and likely cross-pollinated it with other flora millions of years ago to enhance its medicinal effects,” he went on to say.
Dr. Roy Casimir, chief researcher at the Holloway Bioscience Institute, echoed Ram Tah’s statement when asked for comment as part of his continued collaboration with the October Consortium.
“The Consortium continues to provide us with fascinating data. We hope that those medicinal effects will reveal themselves to us over time as we continue to unlock the secrets of this incredible plant.”

articles.title: Frontline Solutions Begins Runner Production
articles.summary: Frontline Solutions has announced the successful supply of critical components needed to complete its initial fleet of Runner vessels, a new craft designed to rapidly transport and deploy mercenary strike teams and their ships to operational locations.
articles.player_impact: Independent pilots who supplied components have enabled the completion of Frontline Solutions' initial Runner fleet. A formal announcement regarding the availability of the expanded mercenary deployment service is expected soon, likely opening new combat and rescue opportunities for registered combatants.
articles.modern_impact: The completion of Frontline Solutions' independently constructed Runner fleet marks a major step in private military logistics. By controlling both the vessels and the deployment infrastructure, Frontline is positioning itself as a fully vertically integrated rapid-response contractor capable of countering organised criminal threats across the core systems without relying on external shipyards.
articles.body_full:
Frontline Solutions has announced the successful supply of critical components needed for the completion of its initial fleet of Runner vessels.
The new craft is capable of rapidly transporting and deploying mercenary strike teams and their ships to operational locations and engage in hostile situations as they arise.
A Frontline Solutions senior technical designer overseeing the production checks stated:
"We are extremely grateful for the support from independent pilots in supplying us with the necessary components to finalise production."
"With the initial Runner fleet now leaving our shipyard for duty trials we're confident that we will meet the demand and be ready to rapidly deploy combat and rescue squads wherever they're needed."
Frontline Solutions are set to make a formal announcement regarding the availability of its expanded service soon.

articles.title: Kestrel Fighter Enters Full Production
articles.summary: Core Dynamics has granted the Kestrel fighter full distribution approval after a limited release, with shipments now reaching shipyards across the core systems. CEO Owen McKenna praised the design team for producing what has become the small fighter of choice for combat pilots.
articles.player_impact: The Kestrel is now available for general purchase at shipyards throughout the core systems. Pilots no longer need to rely on the limited early-release window or travel to Duamta to obtain Core Dynamics' dedicated small combat fighter.
articles.modern_impact: Full production approval cements the Kestrel as Core Dynamics' flagship small fighter and the effective successor to the Eagle Mk II. Its transition from limited release to standard inventory signals that the Federal Navy and independent combat forces are standardising around a new generation of agile, hard-hitting craft, reshaping small-ship combat doctrine across human space.
articles.body_full:
The Kestrel has received the green light for full distribution, having previously been available via limited release only.
Shipments of Core Dynamics’s latest design have begun to arrive at markets. An accompanying press stated the Kestrel has been developed as a highly capable, dedicated combat ship.
CEO Owen McKenna remarked:
“The Kestrel has quickly become the small fighter of choice for combat pilots. We're extremely proud of our engineering and design team.”
The Kestrel is now available for purchase at shipyards throughout the core systems.

articles.title: Federation Breaks Silence on October Accords Exclusion
articles.summary: President Felicia Winters has publicly broken the Federation's silence on its exclusion from the October Accords, expressing disappointment at being denied access to Radicoida unica research and warning that any resulting strategic or technological disadvantage will be treated as a potential threat.
articles.player_impact: No direct call to action for pilots. The statement signals mounting Federal pressure on the October Consortium and may foreshadow future diplomatic, scientific or military moves around HIP 87621 and Radicoida unica research.
articles.modern_impact: Winters' warning is the Federation's first open response to its exclusion from the October Accords and highlights the risk of a superpower-driven research race. The threat of unilateral Federal action could destabilise the fragile corporate custodianship of HIP 87621 and reshape the politics of the enclave.
articles.body_full:
President Felicia Winters conveyed ‘disappointment’ at the Federation’s continued exclusion from Radicoida unica research.
While careful not to criticise members of the October Accords directly, Winters made clear that denying the Federation any level of access to the research and its findings would force the superpower to act:
“We recognise the October Consortium's duty to uphold the Accords it helped establish as a framework for peace in the enclave conflict. However, I would remind Lexi October that the Federation rewards those who choose cooperation."
“Should the outcome of this research put the Federation at a technological or strategic disadvantage against its rivals, my administration will have no choice but to view the situation as a potential threat. That threat will, in turn, dictate our own research priorities.”
Today's press conference from the White House marks the first time the President has spoken openly about the Accords since the conflict for HIP 87621 concluded in February this year.
The Federal Times has reached out to representatives of the members of the October Accords but so far all have declined to comment.

articles.title: Faulcon DeLacy Announces New Ship-Launched ‘Nomad’
articles.summary: Faulcon DeLacy has announced the limited early release of the Nomad, a ship-launched exploration vessel that can operate independently of its mothership and carries an enhanced Mk II Biological Scanner and Mk II Sensor for locating biological surface signals.
articles.player_impact: The Nomad is immediately available as an early-release purchase and will later reach wider shipyard availability. Pilots can use it to explore planetary surfaces and tight terrain without risking their primary ship, and the enhanced biological scanner makes exobiological sampling more efficient.
articles.modern_impact: The Nomad expands the role of ship-launched craft from combat support to independent exploration, potentially changing how pilots survey extreme terrain and collect exobiological data. Its partnership with Vista Genomics for Sanguineous Rim data collection signals growing corporate interest in frontier exobiology.
articles.body_full:
Faulcon DeLacy, the manufacturer behind the popular Python and Cobra ship designs, has announced the limited release of the Nomad.
The Nomad is a ship-launched craft intended to aid explorers in larger ships, allowing them to explore planet surfaces and locations requiring tight manoeuvrability and speed.
Chief of Design, Frank Endis, stated in the press release:
“The Nomad is different to other ship-launched vessels in that it can fly independently of its mothership’s presence. Our team recognised a gap in the market for a smaller craft that grants explorers an alternative option to using their primary ship when navigating difficult terrain.”
“We’re excited to see the most extreme places pilots can take it.”
The Nomad comes with a new Mk II Biological Scanner with an enhanced range and is complemented by a Mk II Sensor for close range signals, allowing pilots to locate biological surface signals directly from the ship.
The Nomad is immediately available as an early-release purchase and will later transition to wider shipyard availability.

articles.title: Frontline Solutions Officially Launches Anti-Crime Deployments
articles.summary: Frontline Solutions has begun deploying mercenary strike teams to anti-crime operations across the core systems using its independently constructed Runner transport fleet, with CEO Imogen le Ray citing the Lhou Mans attacks as a key motivation.
articles.player_impact: Pilots and mercenary teams can sign up at any market port and be deployed via a Runner to available anti-crime operations. This opens lawful mercenary combat and rescue opportunities against organised criminal activity.
articles.modern_impact: The official launch formalises Frontline Solutions' expansion from factional mercenary broker to a vertically integrated anti-crime contractor. The move reflects a broader privatisation of security in the core systems and positions Frontline as a direct counterweight to the Lady Zi pirate coalition.
articles.body_full:
Frontline Solutions has announced that its expanded deployment service has started shipping mercenaries to anti-crime operations across the core systems.
Following the successful manufacturing and test trials of the Runner transport, CEO Imogen le Ray confirmed in a press release that her corporation is ready to deploy strike teams anywhere they are needed, when they are needed, to disrupt organised crime.
“Authorities should no longer have to tackle criminal activities and coordinated piracy with stretched resources, as highlighted in recent events in the Lhou Mans system. With this new service we can augment system security to take on almost any combat or rescue situation.”
Pilots and mercenary teams willing to sign up to an operation should first travel and dock at any market port before being deployed to an available Runner.

articles.title: Vista Genomics Seeks Exploration Data From Sanguineous Rim
articles.summary: Vista Genomics has partnered with Faulcon DeLacy to collect exploration and exobiological data from the Sanguineous Rim, using the new Nomad's capabilities to survey extreme fringe systems and offering bonus payouts for biological samples.
articles.player_impact: Explorers and exobiologists should travel to HD 232819 and register at The Magrathea research megaship before surveying the Sanguineous Rim. Biological samples collected there will earn bonus payouts.
articles.modern_impact: The initiative highlights a shift toward corporate-sponsored frontier exobiology and provides a high-profile test of the Nomad as an exploration platform. It also underscores the value of biological data from the galaxy's outer rim for understanding genetic diversity beyond the core systems.
articles.body_full:
A new exploration initiative from Vista Genomics is aiming to gather data to help assess genetic diversity across the Sanguineous Rim.
To help celebrate the release of the new ship-launched exploration vessel, Faulcon DeLacy has partnered with Vista Genomics in the initiative, calling on independent pilots to help test the Nomad’s capabilities across extreme terrain.
Frank Endis, Chief of Design commented in a statement issued to Vox Galactica that “most exploration efforts naturally head towards the centre of the galaxy. We’re keen to help Vista collect more data from systems on the fringes of the Milky Way.”
Pilots taking part in the initiative will receive a bonus payout for any biological samples found throughout the Sanguineous Rim.
All interested explorers and exobiologists should head to HD 232819 and register at The Magrathea research megaship before heading out into the black.

articles.title: Terri Tora Released by October Consortium in Surprise Move
articles.summary: The October Consortium has unexpectedly released xenobiologist Terri Tora, who had been held since late 3311 after stowing away on a Consortium megaship and bypassing the HIP 87621 permit lock. Chair Lexi October said Tora was fully cooperative and that the changed circumstances following the October Accords made continued detention unnecessary.
articles.player_impact: No direct call to action. Tora's release resolves one of the lingering humanitarian threads of the HIP 87621 mystery, but access to Radicoida unica research remains governed by the October Accords.
articles.modern_impact: The release removes a long-running grievance used to pressure the October Consortium, though Tora's insistence that discoveries like Radicoida unica should not be kept secret reinforces concerns about corporate control of scientific knowledge. The move may be a gesture of goodwill, but its timing amid Federal threats leaves the Accords' stability uncertain.
articles.body_full:
Terri Tora, the xenobiologist credited with triggering widespread interest in the HIP 87621 system, has been released.
Tora, who has been held in custody by October Consortium since her disappearance in late 3311, was investigating rumours of a significant xenobiological discovery when she stowed away on a Consortium megaship. She was later discovered in HIP 87621, having circumnavigated the system’s permit lock, and incarcerated on charges of corporate espionage.
Speaking directly to Vox Galactica, Lexi October said that Tora had been “fully cooperative in questioning” following the security breach and recognised that recent events leading to the signing of the Accords had meant it was time to release her without further charges.
Tora issued the following statement:
“Well, that was an adventure I can tell you! I am relieved to be finally free and to know that things worked out in the end. It was a scary situation to be in.”
“I hadn’t considered the ramifications of my actions until fighting broke out across the surrounding systems. However, the supposed value of Radicoida wasn’t my concern - my only motive was knowledge. Discoveries like this aren’t meant to be kept a secret!”
Tora was met by colleague Professor Frank Raddix, who initially tipped off pilots about her absence, at Exogene Sciences. The pair then departed under October Accord escort.

articles.title: Vista Genomics Exobiology Initiative Deemed a Success
articles.summary: Vista Genomics and Faulcon DeLacy have concluded their Sanguineous Rim exobiology initiative successfully. Pilots gathered extensive biological data and confirmed that the Nomad's Mk II Biological Scanner and Mk II Sensor improve planetary exploration and sampling efficiency.
articles.player_impact: The initiative is complete, so no further signup is needed. The Nomad remains available as an exclusive purchase and will later move to standard shipyard inventories. Participants can expect payouts for their biological samples.
articles.modern_impact: The successful trial validates the Nomad as a practical platform for long-range exobiology and strengthens the corporate partnership between Vista Genomics and Faulcon DeLacy. It also demonstrates growing corporate investment in frontier genetic-diversity research beyond the core systems.
articles.body_full:
Vista Genomics has confirmed the successful conclusion of its exobiology initiative across the Sanguineous Rim.
In partnership with Faulcon DeLacy, both confirmed that pilots not only secured vast quantities of exobiological data needed to investigate genetic diversity across the region but also helped confirm that the Nomad improved planetary exploration.
Chief Engineer Frank Endis, who supervised the campaign for Faulcon DeLacy, reported that the Nomad “allowed for more efficient exobiology sampling and research to be conducted than previously experienced by explorers.”
“The new Mk II Biological Scanner and Mk II Sensor modules that the Nomad provides also offered explorers and exobiologists more productive journeys thanks to their enhanced range capabilities.” he added.
With the trials now concluded, Faulcon DeLacy hopes that the Nomad will quickly become a key feature of long-range exploration and exobiology expeditions for those who own ships that can equip the vessel.
The Nomad is currently available for exclusive purchase initially and will transition to standard shipyard inventories at a later date.

articles.title: Major Corporations Promote Colonia Celebrations
articles.summary: Major core-systems corporations, including Lakon Spaceways, have voiced support for Colonia's tenth-anniversary celebrations, as Jaques and the Colonia Council reveal plans for a galaxy-wide "Colonia Fair" exposition.
articles.player_impact: Pilots can expect a major transportation effort of commodities and rare goods from the core systems to Colonia ahead of the anniversary, hinting at upcoming community logistics activity tied to the "Colonia Fair".
articles.modern_impact: Corporate endorsement from established core-systems players like Lakon Spaceways signals Colonia's evolution from an accidental frontier settlement into a recognised partner within the wider galactic economy, deepening the ties forged a decade earlier by Jaques Station's misjump.
articles.body_full:
Multiple corporations have supported the recent announcement of Colonia’s tenth anniversary celebrations.
Vox Galactica business correspondent Marlon Royce spoke to several representatives of major names from the technology, transport, mining and tourism industries.
“Colonia stands as a beacon of human achievement in deep space,” commented Naomi Landseer, chairperson of Lakon Spaceways. “Lakon Spaceways is synonymous with success out in the black, and we applaud the continued success of Colonia’s people.”
Meanwhile, Jaques and the Colonia Council gave Vox Galactica more behind-the-scenes information about planned festivities.
“It’s high time the corporations in the core systems showered us with some love and attention,” Jaques said enthusiastically from his bar. “So, we’re inviting them to help us pull together the first ‘Colonia Fair’ - a galaxy-sized exposition that’ll include exhibitions, activities, performances, films, art, food...and plenty of libations!”
Vox Galactica understands that preparations are underway for a massive transportation effort of commodities and rare goods from across the core systems to Colonia, with details of the logistics to be announced soon.

frank-raddix.name: Frank Raddix
frank-raddix.bio: Frank Raddix is a scientist in the Elite Dangerous universe, active from 3311-09-02 to 3311-09-25. Closely associated with October Consortium. Professor Frank Raddix's appeal to find missing exobiologist Terri Tora led thousands of pilots to the permit-locked HIP 87621. Professor Frank Raddix demanded clarity on Terri Tora's fate as journalist Alexei Keel published evidence linking the HIP 87621 permit lock to Lexi October.
frank-raddix.bio_full: Professor Frank Raddix is a scientist and colleague of xenobiologist Terri Tora. In 3311 he raised the alarm about Tora's disappearance, leading thousands of pilots to the permit-locked HIP 87621 system. In July 3312 he met Tora at Exogene Sciences after the October Consortium unexpectedly released her from custody, and the pair departed under October Accord escort.

nomad.name: Nomad
nomad.bio_full: The Nomad is a ship-launched exploration vessel developed by Faulcon DeLacy and released in a limited early launch in June 3312. Unlike conventional ship-launched fighters, the Nomad can operate independently of its mothership, allowing pilots to survey tight terrain and planetary surfaces without risking their primary vessel. It is equipped with an enhanced Mk II Biological Scanner and an Mk II Sensor for detecting biological surface signals at close range. The design was marketed specifically at explorers operating larger ships, and the craft was field-tested in partnership with Vista Genomics during an exploration initiative in the Sanguineous Rim. In July 3312 the initiative was deemed a success, with pilots confirming that the Nomad and its scanner and sensor modules made exobiology sampling and research more efficient than previous explorer setups.

nadya-holdstock.name: Nadya Holdstock
nadya-holdstock.bio_full:
"You can fuel a ship with anything that burns. The question is whether you want to arrive."

Nadya Holdstock is a fuel specialist and technician who joined the Distant Worlds 3 expedition with practical knowledge and zero tolerance for shortcuts. Before launch she worked on 15 G. Caeli, buying tech and supplies for the expedition carriers and managing inventory from Old Worlds trading clans. When Commander LilacLight found the derelict prototype, Holdstock was among the first to examine the residue — nanite compounds, strange filaments, crew remains partially consumed by something the logs could not name. She connected the find to a broader pattern of ancient technology resurfacing in modern space. Not academically. Practically. The kind of knowledge that comes from handling dangerous materials daily and learning which ones bite.

Holdstock also worked with Doctor Gery during the Rainbow's End quarantine, helping establish protocols for material that had no business existing in the 3310s. She never wrote papers about it. Just kept the tanks full and the crew alive.

cmdr-drew-wagar.name: CMDR Drew Wagar
cmdr-drew-wagar.bio_full: In July 3306, CMDR Drew Wagar led an expedition aboard the carrier Shekinah — later renamed the Fimbulthul — to revisit the derelict megaship Zurara in the Formidine Rift. The voyage was part of a broader resurgence of interest in Generation Ships and the dark history of the Rift, a region already infamous for the disappearance of the Dynasty Expedition decades earlier. Wagar's work helped connect the scattered fragments of that mystery, tracing the trail of abandoned vessels and encrypted logs that remain a touchstone for deep-space explorers investigating the darker chapters of pre-Federation expansion.

runner.name: Runner
runner.bio: Runner is a vessel class developed by Frontline Solutions for rapid transport and deployment of mercenary strike teams and their ships to operational locations. First announced in June 3312 as part of Frontline's expanded anti-criminal services, the Runner fleet was independently constructed to avoid reliance on external manufacturers. By 3312-06-18, the initial Runner fleet completed production and began duty trials.
runner.bio_full: The Runner is a dedicated squad-deployment vessel developed by Frontline Solutions. It is designed to carry mercenary strike teams together with their ships to hostile or remote locations, allowing rapid response to emerging criminal or rescue scenarios. Frontline Solutions chose to build the Runner fleet independently, maintaining full control over its logistics and manufacturing chain. The first vessels completed production in mid-June 3312 and entered duty trials shortly thereafter. On 3312-06-30, Frontline officially launched anti-crime deployments using the Runner fleet, shipping mercenaries to operations across the core systems.

john.name: John
john.bio_full: "John" is the familiar name by which the founder of the Distant Worlds 3 expedition is known among his inner circle. See the full profile under John Ermitage.

hd-232819.name: HD 232819
hd-232819.bio_full: HD 232819 is a system serving as the registration and staging point for the Vista Genomics and Faulcon DeLacy exploration initiative in the Sanguineous Rim. Pilots participating in the survey are directed to register at The Magrathea research megaship in this system before heading out to collect biological samples from the rim's fringe systems. The initiative was later deemed a success, validating the Nomad and its Mk II Biological Scanner and Mk II Sensor for frontier exobiology.

john-ermitage.name: John Ermitage
john-ermitage.bio_full: Few figures in the modern exploration community carry the weight of history that John Ermitage does. An elderly strategist with tinted glasses and a calm, almost severe bearing, he was brought out of semi-stasis in 3311 to direct the Distant Worlds 3 expedition toward Orion — a route chosen not merely for its scientific promise but to monitor the volatile region around Collinder 70. Ermitage's past is entangled with the final days of GalCop; he claims to have died once and lived under an assumed identity to escape the attention of "reporters and lawyers and hitmen." He distrusts modern COVAS systems, preferring the physical levers and buttons of his vintage Lanner-class vessel, and his network of contacts extends from the Turners on Alioth to figures in the Pilots Federation who still remember the pre-Federation era. Beneath the public face of DW3 as a civilian exploration endeavour, Ermitage orchestrated a concealed agenda: the recovery and repurposing of abandoned GalCop deep space monitoring arrays from the Equinox Project at Sarasvati, the investigation of witch-space harmonic anomalies, and the placement of trusted personnel — including the enigmatic Lya — at critical points in the expedition chain of command. After the expedition he met with Cal in Tianve to discuss the Caretaker Protocol, an apparent remnant of GalCop-era AI research linked to hyperspace bleeding and matter manipulation.

alistair-brodey.name: Alistair Brodey
alistair-brodey.bio_full: Alistair Brodey is an independent deep-space pilot who flew an Eagle with an engineered wake scanner during the Distant Worlds 3 expedition. While the fleet was near Colonia, Brodey detected a cross-band echo at fifteen cycles — a harmonic anomaly that later proved significant in tracing lost expedition vessels. Hermine Delarue knew him by reputation, suggesting he was no stranger to the exploration community's more difficult operations. Brodey's technical skill with wake scanning and his willingness to fly a lightly armed Eagle into uncertain signal territory exemplify the kind of independent operator who has always filled the gaps between official survey programmes.

timotheus-haddard.name: Timotheus Haddard
timotheus-haddard.bio_full: "Timotheus Haddard" and "Quartermaster Timotheus Haddard" refer to the same individual — the logistics officer who kept the Distant Worlds 3 fleet operational across its four-month trek. See the full profile under Quartermaster Timotheus Haddard.

october-consortium.name: October Consortium
october-consortium.bio: October Consortium is a organization active in Elite Dangerous lore from 3307-10-05 to 3312-04-30. Frequently associated with HIP 87621, Holloway Bioscience Institute. Key activities include: Aegis confirms that special advisor Seo Jin-ae has taken a hiatus from her duties.; Professor Frank Raddix's appeal to find missing exobiologist Terri Tora led thousands of pilots to the permit-locked HIP 87621.
october-consortium.bio_full:
The October Consortium is a corporate organisation controlled by billionaire investor Lexi October, known primarily for its controversial stewardship of the HIP 87621 system. The Consortium acquired permit rights to the system over a decade ago and maintained it as a closed research zone, blocking colonisation within a 37-light-year radius and restricting access to all but its own scientific teams.

In 3311, the Consortium came under intense scrutiny after long-range scans detected anomalous exobiological readings in HIP 87621. Lexi October defended her organisation's legal ownership and questioned why rival billionaire Zachary Rackham had failed to share data from his galaxy-wide exploration campaign. When the Pilots' Federation brokered exclusive access for licensed Commanders, the Consortium dismissed data inconsistencies as "spoofing" and banned fleet carriers permanently. The October Consortium's opaque management of HIP 87621 made it a focal point for scientific intrigue and eventual superpower military confrontation. By June 3312, Federal President Felicia Winters had broken the Federation's public silence over its exclusion from the October Accords, directly warning Lexi October that continued denial of Radicoida unica access would be treated as a potential threat. In July 3312, the Consortium unexpectedly released detained xenobiologist Terri Tora, stating that she had been cooperative in questioning and that the changed circumstances following the Accords made continued detention unnecessary.

holloway-bioscience-institute.name: Holloway Bioscience Institute
holloway-bioscience-institute.bio: Holloway Bioscience Institute is a research active in Elite Dangerous lore from 3305-02-07 to 3312-04-15. Frequently associated with HIP 87621, October Consortium. Key activities include: *Pilots Federation ALERT* The Holloway Bioscience Institute has rewarded pilots who delivered living matter extracted from space-dwelling organisms.; The superpowers agree to shut down Aegis permanently and establish independent anti-xeno taskforces.
holloway-bioscience-institute.bio_full:
The Holloway Bioscience Institute is a scientific research organisation dedicated to the study of xenological life forms. In February 3305, Dr Roy Casimir announced plans to construct a dedicated research centre in the Nahuaru system to analyse new life forms discovered through the Codex, requesting construction materials and exploration data from independent pilots.

The Institute later became involved in broader Thargoid research, with senior member Dr Jeong-Hui Shin contributing to academic debates about Thargoid behaviour following the Proteus Wave disaster in 3308. The Holloway Bioscience Institute's work expanded humanity's biological knowledge beyond the Thargoid focus, studying the diverse alien ecosystems that pilots encountered across the galaxy.

python.name: Python
python.bio: Python is a technology in the Elite Dangerous universe, mentioned from 3301-05-05 to 3301-05-05. Developed or used by Zaonce Jet Gang, Alliance Elite Diplomatic Corps, Silver United Solutions. To celebrate, Silver United organised a discount on all Faulcon DeLacy ships at Ridley Scott Station, including a limited number of Pythons.
python.bio_full: The Python is a multi-role starship manufactured by Faulcon DeLacy, widely regarded as one of the most versatile vessels available to independent pilots. Its balanced performance and generous internal compartments have made it a popular choice for trading, mining, combat, and exploration. The Python name is also associated with the Python Mk II, a later variant developed around Achilles Aerospace's Supercruise Overcharge Frame Shift Drive.

uwe-toramund.name: Uwe Toramund
uwe-toramund.bio_full:
Stoic. Precise. Unflappable in the presence of Ram Tah's volcanic eyebrows.

Uwe Toramund is the senior lab assistant at Phoenix Base on Meene — a position that sounds modest until you understand what Ram Tah demands of his staff. Toramund conducted the measurements that revealed the Guardian frequency anomaly: eight sites, six traditional channels gone dark, one pico-hertz signal in the gravity-wave range. He checked for glitches. Rechecked. Checked again. "It's not a conclusion, Ram. It's physical. You can measure it."

That sentence changed the expedition's trajectory. Because if the Guardian network was degrading, every ship module derived from Guardian technology — boosters, weapons, shields — was running on borrowed time. Toramund did not celebrate the discovery. He updated his holofac and waited for the next assignment. The Guardians would not have understood his calm. Humans, after all, panic differently than machines.

isolde-rochester.name: Isolde Rochester
isolde-rochester.bio: Isolde Rochester is a president in the Elite Dangerous universe, active from 3310-10-31 to 3310-10-31. Closely associated with Core Dynamics. Princess Aisling Duval announces her engagement to Federal Ambassador Jordan Rochester at a press conference on Emerald. Reactions to Princess Aisling Duval's engagement to Ambassador Jordan Rochester range across the political spectrum.

doctor-gery.name: Doctor Gery
doctor-gery.bio_full:
Doctor Gery appeared at Rainbow's End during the expedition's most precarious hour. Medical credentials, certainly. But the questions he asked were not clinical.

He examined the nanite-compound residue recovered from the derelict prototype carrier. He studied the strange filaments that had partially consumed crew bodies. And he listened — really listened — when Jasmina Halsey described what the Caretakers had shown her in witch-space. Gery's assessment was blunt: the technology involved operated on principles that modern medical science could not model, let alone treat. He recommended quarantine protocols stricter than anything DSS had planned. Then he helped implement them, working alongside Alessia Verdi and Jacky Hew in a makeshift lab that had no business processing material that dangerous.

Whether Gery was assigned by Deep Space Surveys, recruited by Ermitage's network, or simply showed up because someone needed to — the records do not say. Some specialists prefer it that way.
